Preface

This volume marks the revival of a resolution that directs the GBC to publish an annual up-to-date corpus of the Society's laws. It is also a significant step on the way to the drafting of a constitution for ISKCON, which Srila Prabhupada asked the GBC to put together in the early seventies. Finally, this volume will serve the GBC, ISKCON Leaders and all devotees as a useful source book of information in the practical affairs of executing devotional service within our institution. It is the hope of the GBC Body that the Vaisnavas in Srila Prabhupada's great movement will be satisfied with this compilation of ISKCON Law.

There may be laws that are obsolete, redundant, contradictory or poorly composed. And there are undoubtedly areas that our laws do not cover sufficiently. But in general, these laws are well thought out, each one representing many hours of deliberation on the part of many of the most experienced devotees in ISKCON. To get us from this corpus to a constitution, the help of all interested devotees throughout the movement is welcome.

-H.H. Suhotra Swami (GBC 2nd Vice Chairman 1997-98)

1 International Society for Krishna Consciousness

1.1 Definition

The International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) is the spiritual institution founded by His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada in July 1966 as a continuation of the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya sampradaya. ISKCON was personally directed by its Founder-Acarya Srila Prabhupada until his departure on November 14, 1977. According to Srila Prabhupada's will, ISKCON continued thereafter under the ultimate managing authority of the Governing Body Commission (GBC).

Accordingly, ISKCON is that institution founded by Srila Prabhupada and originally directed by him, which continues to be directed after his departure by the GBC.

1.2 Principles: The Seven Purposes of ISKCON

1. To systematically propagate spiritual knowledge to society at large and to educate all peoples in the techniques of spiritual life in order to check the imbalance of values in life, and to achieve real unity and peace in the world.

2. To propagate consciousness of Krsna as it is revealed in the Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam.

3. To bring the members of the Society together with each other and nearer to Krsna, the prime entity, and thus develop the idea within the members and humanity at large that each soul is part and parcel of the quality of Godhead (Krsna).

4. To teach and encourage the sankirtana movement of congregational chanting of the holy name of God as revealed in the teachings of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu.

5. To erect for the members, and for society at large, a holy place of transcendental pastimes, dedicated to the Personality of Krsna.

6. To bring the members closer together for the purpose of teaching a simpler and more natural way of life.

7. With a view towards achieving the aforementioned purposes, to publish and distribute periodicals, magazines, books, and other writings.

307.4 · Ban of 'One Time Use' Plastic (2019)

ISKCON — other
[Guideline]

(Proposed by Hrdaya Caitanya Das, sponsored by him and Devamrita Swami)
Whereas plastic is often used once-off and then thrown away;
Whereas the lifetime of plastic varies from 50 years to more than 1000 years;
Whereas plastic contaminates mother earth and her inhabitants;
Whereas many ISKCON temples use plastic and foam cups, plates, spoons, water bottles, maha-
prasadam packages, plastic bags, etc., once-off and then discard them despite there being
biodegradable alternatives;
Whereas Srila Prabhupada states that first you become conscious and then you become Krishna
conscious;
Whereas there is an increasing awareness in the general public about such issues and ISKCON
should set a proper example:
Resolved:
That ISKCON centres and members are strongly encouraged to not use single-use plastic.

307.04 · ISKCON’s statement on race (2021)

ISKCON — other: General
[Statement]

Whereas ISKCON needs to reinforce its position on race;

RESOLVED:
That ISKCON’s global Governing Body Commission (GBC) issues the following as ISKCON’s official
position statement on race:

In this time of global strife, tension, and polarization, the insights expressed in the Bhagavad Gita, a
timeless wisdom text, irrevocably establish the spiritual equality of all beings. Such equality fosters
tolerance, understanding, deep compassion, and unity in diversity. Moreover, Sri Isopanisad says,
“He who systematically sees everything in relation to the Supreme Lord, who sees all living entities
as His parts and parcels, and who sees the Supreme Lord within everything never hates anything or
any being.” In this way, all living beings are souls, children of God, brothers and sisters in God’s all-
embracing family.

In the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition, of which the International Society for Krishna Consciousness
(ISKCON) is a present-day branch, inclusiveness has been taught by generations of teachers,
including Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1534), the pioneer of a great social and religious
movement that began five centuries ago in India. Despite forceful opposition, Sri Caitanya
Mahaprabhu, who is understood by the tradition to be Lord Krishna (God) Himself, opened his
movement to everyone.

In turn, His Divine Grace A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, (1896‒1977), ISKCON’s
Founder-Acharya, travelled the world to establish ISKCON and spread the message of bhakti, or
unconditional love of God, and to teach that spiritually we are all equal. Hence, Sri Caitanya’s vision
of equality and inclusiveness underpins ISKCON’s worldview.

Srila Prabhupada tirelessly proclaimed the physical body to be like an outward dress and the spirit
soul to be the real person. He taught that material differences were external and superficial. What
matters is the person, not the dress — the soul, not the body. On the spiritual plane of the soul,
equality is true and absolute. In this way, his teachings pivoted on spirit, not matter. They went far

12
beyond the considerations of body, mind, intellect, and false ego to culminate in pure devotion and
service to God, which only begins in earnest when our sense of who we are is firmly removed from
any bodily, psychological, or intellectual designation.

Through his prolific writings, lectures, and organizational designs, Srila Prabhupada tirelessly
endeavored to assist everyone in rekindling this vision and their natural love and in refining the
kindness, integrity, and happiness that ensue. He placed love and compassion at the center of his
personal dealings, and he exemplified these divine qualities in the way he inspired and directed the
communities and organizations he founded. He taught that traits such as sex, race, and social class
are ultimately irrelevant. His efforts were heroic; his accomplishments profound.

Clearly, such a sublime, spiritual vision warmly embraces all communities and races. Indeed,
ISKCON, or the Hare Krishna movement, is committed to this vision and therefore invites everyone
to participate and share fellowship in service to God, take responsibility, and hold positions of
spiritual leadership.

Thus, the Hare Krishna movement stands against any form of racial bigotry and discrimination and
condemns any behavior that is derogatory, demeaning, and racially insensitive. Instead, it
encourages racial harmony and spiritual equality, as did Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu and Srila
Prabhupada. We are committed to creating an environment in which everyone feels valued and is
educated to manifest a culture of universal peace, understanding, respect, tolerance, friendliness,
and forgiveness. Furthermore, we remain committed to intervening, wherever and whenever
necessary within ISKCON, to stop any wrongdoing that opposes such values.

Let us all acknowledge our shared spirituality, transcend racial differences and divides, and together
live up to aspirations worthy of our ultimate connectedness with every living being, and with God.

Whereas a concise statement of siddhanta for ISKCON would help establish the philosophical unity of our
movement, allowing for diversity of practical application;

301.7 · Letter of Appreciation to Guru Gauranga Das (2019)

ISKCON Members

Dear Guru Gauranga Prabhu,
Please accept our humble obeisances. All glories to Srila Prabhupada.
On behalf of the GBC Body, we respectfully offer you the title of GBC Emeritus with gratitude and
appreciation for your years of contributions and services to ISKCON and dedication to Srila
Prabhupada.
You pioneered Krishna consciousness and laid the foundation for ISKCON’s future growth in
Switzerland in 1971, later establishing ISKCON as a legally recognized Swiss Church foundation.
Thereafter, you organized Srila Prabhupada’s official reception by the Government of Geneva and, in
1978, organized the first public Rathayatra in a major European city outside the UK.
Later, you successfully resisted defamatory remarks (libel) made by the Catholic Church against the
Hare Krishna movement in Switzerland, and thereby defended the position of ISKCON as a bona fide
spiritual organization.
You were appointed to the GBC Body in 1986, and served as the first GBC Minister of Justice. During
your tenure, you established ISKCON’s first Conflict Resolution Procedures (CRP).
Recently, you worked tirelessly to lead the legal team that successfully sued to prevent the sale of the
Sri Sri Radha-Govinda Temple in New York and restored it to its rightful place in ISKCON.
We thank you very much for your past and present services that have brought much benefit and
protection to our society.
Your servants,
Madhu Sevita Das
Bhaktivaibhava Swami
Ramai Swami
(GBC Executive Committee, on behalf of the GBC Body)

301.06 · GBC decision concerning Ananda Caitanya dasa’s appeal (2020)

ISKCON members

Action order
Whereas Ananda Caitanya dasa (BCAIS), formerly Bhakti Swarupa Caitanya Swami, was found to have
committed serious transgressions of the sannyasa order
Whereas the Sannyasa Committee, considering the evidence in this regard, decided to divest him of his
sannyasa title
Whereas Ananda Caitanya dasa subsequently appealed this decision
Whereas the GBC appointed a subcommittee consisting of Giriraja Swami, Krsna Kesava dasa, and Radha
dasi (MG) to look into this matter further
Whereas the subcommittee has submitted its recommendations to the GBC Body
RESOLVED:
That Ananda Caitanya dasa is directed to comply with the following:
1. Regular close association and careful mentoring by senior devotees. Such help should be
specific in assisting Ananda Caitanya dasa to value the reputation of Srila Prabhupada,
ISKCON, the sannyasa order, and the devotee community. He has indicated that Niranjana
Swami and Bhakti Caitanya Swami know him and could be effective mentors.
2. Sannyasa status suspended for a minimum of four years. This suspension would run from the
date of the original decision, meaning that Ananda Caitanya dasa has served one year of
suspension thus far. At the end of the four-year period, his status should be reviewed by the
Sannyasa Committee. If he is not ready for reinstatement, the Sannyasa Committee may extend
the suspension after consideration of feedback from Ananda Caitanya dasa's mentors.
3. Limited preaching opportunities. After a period of one year from the adoption of these
recommendations, Ananda Caitanya dasa could be given the opportunity to preach at small
home gatherings. If this opportunity is granted to him, we recommend that he be required to
obtain the permission of local and regional leaders in the area (after disclosing the terms of the
decision against him). In addition, he should be chaperoned by a mature and reliable Vaisnava
during any travel or preaching. At the end of four years from the date of the original decision, his
mentors can assess whether he is ready to preach on a wider scale.
4. Five-year ban on leadership positions. This was part of the original decision and we believe it is
appropriate. This five-year period would begin from the date of the original decision. The general
standard used by both the Child Protection Office and the North American Leader Misconduct
Committee is that giving Srimad-Bhagavatam class, giving the Sunday Feast or other public
lectures, or leading kirtana are leadership positions.
5. Further restrictions possible. It should be made clear to Ananda Caitanya dasa that this remedial
program of rectification is an opportunity for him to restore trust and to be reinstated as a
recognized ISKCON sannyasi. If he breaches the conditions of probation, then his probationary
period should be extended or he should receive further restrictions, including perhaps
permanent removal of sannyasa status.
This GBC decision is based on two primary considerations. First, rectification and reintegration are
important goals of any system of correction in ISKCON. Ananda Caitanya dasa's offenses do not warrant
his being excluded from ISKCON. Thus, we must be concerned with reforming him.
6
Further, a five-year period of prohibition with no mentoring or assessment means that we will have no
assurance that Ananda Caitanya dasa has rectified those tendencies that led to this situation. A shorter
period of restrictions with careful mentoring and monitoring is more likely to achieve good results.

303.03 · Enhancing the culture of reading Srila Prabhupada's books globally (2020)

ISKCON temples and affiliates

via Srila Prabhupada’s book reading week — 2020
Action Order
Whereas there is evidence that ISKCON devotees, including leaders, often face challenges in regularly
reading Srila Prabhupada's books
Whereas at the 2017 edition of the SGGS it was also felt there should be a worldwide effort to increase
reading of Srila Prabhupada’s books
Whereas Srila Prabhupada had many times emphasized the importance of his books and requested the
leaders of ISKCON to read his books and train others to systematically study his books
Whereas Srila Prabhupada often made statements such as, “I am very glad to know that you are reading
our literatures and you are very thoughtful about them”, and “In my books the philosophy of Krishna
Consciousness is explained fully so if there is anything which you do not understand, then you simply have
to read again and again”
Whereas Srila Prabhupada cautioned his followers to daily employ their intelligence, by reading, discussing
and preaching to others, in order to keep our minds and actions pure
Whereas there is the need to bequeath to future generations of ISKCON a culture of diligently reading Srila
Prabhupada’s books, so as to prevent speculations and concoctions
Whereas by reading Srila Prabhupada’s books regularly, present and future generations can gain Srila
Prabhupada’s divine association
RESOLVED:
The week leading up to Srila Prabhupada’s arrival in America be declared “Srila Prabhupada’s Book
Reading Week.” This year this falls between September 3 and 9.
● During this week ISKCON centers are encouraged to highlight the importance of reading Srila
Prabhupada’s books in all lectures, addresses and discussions.
● During this week ISKCON leaders are encouraged to inspire devotees under their care to read Srila
Prabhupada’s books by organizing orientation sessions and seminars on how and why to read Srila
Prabhupada’s books regularly and systematically.
● New programs may be introduced that will encourage and allow congregation devotees to take up
the reading of Srila Prabhupada’s books enthusiastically.

303.03 · Dates for 2022 GBC Annual General Meeting — 2021 (2020)

GBC Meetings: Annual General Meeting

Whereas the Srimad-Bhagavatam, Sri Caitanya-caritamrta or Bhagavad-gita class is a sacred time
dedicated to reading, discussing and deepening our understanding of our scriptures
Whereas the advertising of one’s own devotional products during or at the end of giving the Srimad-
Bhagavatam, Sri Caitanya-caritamrta or Bhagavad-gita class is in poor taste
Whereas it has been observed over the last few years, when tuning into many online classes around the
world, that this practice is gathering pace and risks becoming the norm
Whereas speakers who wish to promote their own devotional products, should, ahead of time, arrange with
the relevant authority to inform the devotees where—after class—their book, CD or USB stick etc., will be
available for purchase
RESOLVED:
No books, paraphernalia or any other products will be allowed to be advertised, promoted, or sold from or
near the speaker’s asana before, during, or after the class
All ISKCON temples and centers will thus ensure that when speaking from the speaker’s asana, speakers
will not use the speaker’s asana or nearby as a platform for the promotion, advertising or sale of any books,
paraphernalia or other products including their own.
The only exceptions to this law are the books and recordings of Srila Prabhupada.

303.03 · Cooking with ghee (2020)

ISKCON temples and affiliates

Guideline
Whereas Srila Prabhupada personally instructed and taught his disciples to prepare prasadam using ghee
Whereas most of our ISKCON temples are using oils instead of ghee for cooking, mainly due to economic
reasons
Whereas Srila Prabhupada stated:
“Anna, ghṛta, dadhi and dugdha are food grains, ghee, yogurt and milk. Actually, these are the basis
of all food. Vegetables and fruits are subsidiary... We should understand that in order to prepare
nutritious food, we require only grains, ghee, yogurt and milk. We cannot offer anything else to the
Deity. The Vaiṣṇava, the perfect human being, does not accept anything not offered to the Deity.”
(Purport Cc Madhya 4.93)
Whereas Srila Prabhupada stated:
“There should be abundant prasadam for whoever comes all day long. The kitchen should go on.
So see there is sufficient stock of rice, atta, ghee, etc. The life members should be especially cared
for and invited.” (Letter to Gurudas July 1, 1974 Melbourne)
Whereas Srila Prabhupada stated:
8
“From the very beginning I was asking to open restaurant and farm. Produce ghee in the farm and
send to the restaurant, and make nice samosā, kachorī preparation, and there will be no scarcity of
money. And if you organize in this way, your whole country will be transferred into Kṛṣṇa conscious
country. Whole country.” (Room Conversation -- May 4, 1976, Honolulu)
Whereas Srila Prabhupada personally made multiple arrangements for providing ghee at various ISKCON
temples
Whereas Srila Prabhupada stated:
“No society can improve in transcendental knowledge without the guidance of such first-class men,
and no brain can assimilate the subtle form of knowledge without fine brain tissues. For such
important brain tissues we require a sufficient quantity of milk and milk preparations.” (Light of the
Bhagavata 27)
Whereas Srila Prabhupada made statements stressing ghee as an unavoidable essential in the diet for
development of necessary intellect
RESOLVED:
All ISKCON Temples are encouraged to use ghee in their cooking.

306.02 · Mayapur Festival declaration: Section A — Statement of commitment (2020)

International Projects

— 2020
Statement
Whereas Srila Prabhupada showed by his own personal example the importance of the Mayapur Festival
by attending every year—being the first one to arrive and the last one to depart
Whereas Srila Prabhupada encouraged devotees to participate in the Mayapur Festival
Whereas Srila Prabhupada expects his GBC to be “Acarya-like” and set an example
Whereas ISKCON Mayapur is our world headquarters, and the home of the Temple of the Vedic
Planetarium (TOVP). Thus, an ideal location is provided here for the GBC to associate with other ISKCON
devotees by engaging in the five principal limbs of bhakti together
Whereas by performing devotional activities together in Sri Dham Mayapur, we shall create a universal
impact. It was none other than Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur who said that, “. . . just by the performance of
Navadvipa Mandala Parikrama the world can be liberated”
Whereas the mood and action of the current leaders will send a message to future generations of leaders
Whereas the Mayapur Festival is an opportunity to foster love, trust, and friendship. The family that prays
together, stays together
Whereas a source of frustration for some devotees is to travel to Mayapur and not be able to associate with
the leaders, due to our leaders being too busy during the GBC meetings, and their rapid departure from
Mayapur after the meetings
Whereas if the Mayapur Festival is not well attended by our leaders, this will be a big loss for our society
RESOLVED:
9
That the GBC Body makes the following statement:
“The GBC Body is committed to a healthy and wholesome Mayapur Festival. To achieve this end, we
commit to supporting this festival through our personal participation, as well as encouraging our fellow
Vaisnavas to participate.”

ISKCON
worldwide — 2021

301.06 · GBC decision concerning Ananda Caitanya dasa’s appeal (2021)

ISKCON members: Individual devotees
[Administrative order]

Whereas Ananda Caitanya dasa (BCAIS) and the lady with whom he had a relationship confessed that,
while he was a sannyasi, they engaged in illicit sex on a number of occasions;

Whereas Ananda Caitanya dasa, on numerous occasions, even during interviews in a formal investigation
into his actions, lied concerning the allegations of his deviations as a sannyasi;

Whereas Ananda Caitanya dasa committed numerous offenses against those conducting the investigation
into his actions;

Whereas Ananda Caitanya dasa violated the terms of his probation as given in GBC resolution (301.6 of
2020)

RESOLVED:
Two committees will be formed to monitor Ananda Caitanya dasa.

The first committee, an International committee, will be comprised of Bhakti Vijnana Goswami, Bhakti
Caitanya Swami, Caitanya Candra Carana dasa, and Acyutatma dasa. This Committee will monitor Ananda

9
Caitanya dasa’s general behavior and his adherence to the GBC’s decision and restrictions resulting from
his deviations.

The second committee, a Local committee, will be comprised of the Lithuanian national leadership headed
by Dhruvananda dasa. This committee will monitor Ananda Caitanya dasa’s services and adherence to the
GBC resolution in Lithuania.

Ananda Caitanya dasa will remain in Lithuania under the supervision of the local leadership for a period of
two years effective from the date of this resolution. Under their guidance and supervision, he will be
encouraged to serve in whatever capacity they see as appropriate. In Lithuania, during the next two years
effective from the date of this resolution, Ananda Caitanya dasa will not be permitted to give classes,
neither in person nor online nor lead kirtans in any ISKCON temple, ISKCON centre, and/or ISKCON
related organisations and/or congregations in Lithuania.

Ananda Caitanya dasa will be encouraged to serve senior devotees around the world in some non-public
setting, such as translating their lectures off-line.

The Lithuanian leadership will give a semi-annual report and recommendations concerning Ananda
Caitanya dasa to the International committee.

After two years, effective from the date of this resolution, the International and Local committees will decide
on which restrictions in Lithuania, which include, but are not limited to, preaching and leading kirtans will
continued to be imposed on Ananda Caitanya dasa.

It is suggested that the local authorities consider obtaining professional counseling to help Ananda
Caitanya dasa.

GBC Resolution 301.06 of 2020, which dealt with the possible future reinstatement of Ananda Caitanya
dasa as an ISKCON sannyasi, is hereby rescinded.

Outside of Lithuania, Ananda Caitanya dasa, for an indefinite period of time, effective from the date of this
resolution, is not allowed to give classes, lead kirtans, either in person and/or online, or take any leadership
position in any ISKCON temple, ISKCON centre, and/or ISKCON related organisations and/or
congregations worldwide.

The international committee can, after a period of 3 years, effective from the date of this resolution, submit
a request to the GBC that resolution be modified or rescinded.

When wearing dhoti and kurta Ananda Caitanya dasa must not dress in saffron.

Any violations by Ananda Caitanya dasa of any or all of the above restrictions will result in further
disciplinary measures being imposed upon him.

303.03 · Eco-theology and Three Tiers of Eco-Guidelines (2021)

ISKCON temples and affiliates: Guidelines for ISKCON
[Guideline]

temples

Whereas Srila Prabhupada’s Sixth Purpose for ISKCON is to teach a “simpler more natural way of life;”

Whereas the ISKCON Environmental Initiative (IEI) has produced a document “The Eco-theology of Our
Tradition” delineating the importance of environmental awareness and appropriate behaviors for Gaudiya
Vaishnavas and the followers of Srila Prabhupada;
10
Whereas ISKCON communities both urban or rural should be exemplary in upholding the principles of
sattvic lifestyles in all areas, including in their vision, teaching, and management;

Whereas ISKCON communities lack specific guidelines for practical steps to undertake regarding respect
and care for the natural environment;

Whereas the ISKCON Global Duty Officer for the Environment, the ISKCON Environmental Initiative (IEI),
and ISKCON Communications Ministry have developed appropriate guidelines in three tiers, or levels of
application, for temple communities and members;

Whereas such guidelines have been reviewed and endorsed by leading members and managers of
ISKCON who are concerned and knowledgeable in these issues;

Whereas care of the earth is an essential issue facing society-at-large, and there is a significant role for
ISKCON to play in demonstrating care for Lord Krishna’s creation;

Whereas ISKCON communities, members, and the world in general will benefit from the GBC endorsing
such guidelines and encouraging their application within ISKCON.

RESOLVED:
The document “Three Tiers of Environmental Practices” as presented by the ISKCON Environmental
Initiative, the ISKCON Global Duty Officer of the Environment, and the ISKCON Communications Ministry,
and with the endorsement of other global ISKCON leaders and scholars, is hereby adopted as an Official
Guideline for all ISKCON Temples and Communities. The GBC strongly encourages all ISKCON temples,
communities, and projects, and wherever possible individual devotees, to apply the principles and
guidelines in their daily lives and practices. (It is understood that these guidelines may be updated, every 3-
5 years, at the discretion of the GDO of the Environment, the ISKCON Communications Ministry, and the
ISKCON Environmental Initiative.)

Furthermore, the document “Eco-theology of Our Tradition” is recognized by the GBC as providing valuable
insights on the Gaudiya Vaishnava philosophy regarding the need for ISKCON devotees and leaders to
strive to live in harmony with the natural environment, and to respect the natural world as the property and
energy of the Supreme Lord.

[Footnotes to resolution]
Recognizing the document “Eco-theology of Our Tradition” carries no cost.

Adopting the Three Tiers of Environmental Practices as Guidelines may have some initial costs, but will
have a positive short and long term economic impact on local communities.

1. Most Tier One guidelines, such as composting and recycling, will incur no costs. Some guidelines,
such as minimizing waste of food and energy will immediately save money. Some items, such as
stopping the use of environmentally harmful garden products and only using biodegradable plates,
cups, and flatware may incur initial costs but are likely to inspire donors to cover those costs.
2. Some Tier Two guidelines will immediately save money, such as growing more food in temple
gardens. Other items, such as purchasing energy efficient machines and automobiles, will require
upfront costs that will be recovered over time, and save money in the long run.

301.05 · Status of Anirdesya Vapu dasa (formerly known as Bhaktividya Purna (2022)

ISKCON Members: Restricting a devotee’s participation in
[Governing law]

ISKCON
Swami) — 2022

Whereas an October 28 2022 CPO decision determined that Anirdesya Vapu dasa, previously known as
Bhaktividya Purna Swami, had engaged in the sexual abuse, sexual harassment, and psychological abuse
of a child

Whereas it was also confirmed that he had engaged in sexual acts with at least one adult woman over an
extended period of time

Whereas a further investigation by the Guru Services Committee has confirmed the same

Whereas such behaviors are in gross violation of Vaisnava codes of conduct, especially for someone who
is trusted to give spiritual guidance as a leader and a guru. They go against the very principles of care for
the vulnerable which should guide our every action and thought

Whereas in February 2007 Anirdesya Vapu dasa was restricted from accepting disciples via GBC
Resolution 312/B which was based upon a CPO decision from September 2000

Whereas it has been established that Anirdesya Vapu dasa violated that prohibition and initiated devotees
after that date

Whereas based on the 2022 CPO decision, and the new information about the extent of Anirdesya Vapu
dasa’s abuses that it revealed, and his other violations, the GBC Guru Services Committee has determined
that Anirdesya Vapu dasa is unqualified to serve as either a diksa-guru or siksa-guru (initiating disciples, or
offering spiritual instruction)

Whereas the GBC Sannyasa Committee has suspended Anirdesya Vapu dasa’s sannyasa status, and that
is likely to be made permanent in the near future.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

The GBC affirms that Anirdesya Vapu dasa is, for the duration of his life prohibited from:

 Accepting disciples in ISKCON; and
 Serving as a siksa-guru in ISKCON; and
 Giving any form of spiritual guidance or instruction, including leading or contributing to any classes,
meetings, or seminars of any kind, at any ISKCON temple, or affiliated program, festival, venue, or
online forum.
Furthermore, regarding those devotees who accepted initiation from Anirdesya Vapu dasa:

 If such an initiation was before February 2007, those devotees are advised to seek spiritual
guidance from senior devotees in ISKCON and to continue serving within ISKCON as they have
been doing. They continue to be initiated devotees in ISKCON, in the line of Srila Prabhupada, with
the full privileges and responsibilities thereof. Yet, if any of those devotees chooses to seek
reinitiation from a guru in good standing in ISKCON, either now or in the future, they are welcomed
and encouraged to do so. In such a circumstance, devotees should seek further guidance from their
local ISKCON authorities and GBC.
 If such an initiation occurred after February 2007, the date that Anirdesya Vapu dasa was prohibited
from initiating, those devotees are strongly advised to seek initiation from an ISKCON guru in good
standing, as their current initiation status has no standing in ISKCON.

The GBC EC will reach out to ISKCON devotees worldwide, and especially those impacted by Anirdesya
Vapu dasa’s abuse and other actions to share this information and to offer them appropriate spiritual
support.

301.06 · GBC Decision regarding Lokanath Swami (2022)

ISKCON members: Individual devotees
[Statement]

Whereas in 1990 a devotee invited Lokanath Swami to stay with his family for several days while
recovering from a serious injury. The host also “requested Lokanath Swami to train and impart Indian
culture to his youngest daughter, who was eleven and a half years old at the time” (the “minor”)

Whereas the minor alleged to ISKCON’s Governing Body Commission (“GBC Body” or “GBC”) three years
later that Lokanath Swami had touched her inappropriately during his stay in the minor's home

Whereas the GBC took these allegations seriously and immediately launched an investigation, which
included reaching out to the minor and her family. The investigation also included a review by independent
mental health experts. The GBC also imposed certain restrictions on Lokanath Swami

Whereas the minor (then an adult) raised the issue again in 2010, 20 years after the original event(s). The
GBC then reopened the matter and imposed additional restrictions on Lokanath Swami

Whereas there was recently discussion about reopening the Lokanath Swami matter for a third time

Whereas the GBC appointed a Review Panel whose work resulted in the Review Panel Report of the
Lokanath Swami Matter (“the Report”)

Whereas the GBC found the Review Panel’s in-depth and professional Report to be helpful and insightful

Whereas the Review Panel members, unanimously agreed that:

 The allegations concerning Lokanath Swami had been fully investigated in both 1993 and again in
2010-2011
 These investigations were adequately documented
 Lokanath Swami substantially complied with the restrictions imposed on him
 The Lokanath Swami matter be referred back to the GBC to act on the Review Panel’s
recommendations

Whereas the GBC has adopted the resolution “GBC non-intervention in the functioning of its deputed
agencies — 2022", requiring that henceforth any plausible claim of abuse or misconduct be directly referred
to the appropriate ISKCON agency rather than to the GBC Body

Based on ISKCON’s ecclesiastical principles and practices as well as the Report,

Therefore, it is resolved that:
The GBC Body endorses the Review Panel’s recommendation that the Lokanath Swami matter, already
twice adjudicated, not be reopened for further proceedings as no new relevant facts pertaining to this
matter have come to light, as of the date hereof.

The GBC Body reaffirms its existing policy that an ISKCON Regional Governing Body (“RGB”) or similar
body has the right to restrict any devotee from visiting and preaching in their region(s), such as has already
been done in North America.

Lokanath Swami shall not initiate disciples, in person or virtually, in any region or area where he has not
been welcomed by the relevant RGB or similar body of area leaders. In the case of rare exceptions that
may be proposed to the RGB (or similar body), the GBC Executive Committee (“EC”) will assist in reaching
an agreeable outcome.

This present Resolution is based on and limited to the facts described herein.

305.01 · Improving the Review Process of Editorial Revisions Undertaken by (2022)

ISKCON related organizations: Bhaktivedanta Book Trust
[Statement]

(BBT)
the BBT — 2022

Whereas an Editorial Review Panel (ERP) was set up by the BBT, in conjunction with the GBC, in 2019 for
the purpose of reviewing the editorial revisions made by the BBT editors

Whereas a part of the resolution states that “If there is a dispute between the ERP and the BBT Editorial
Board, or for that matter among ERP members themselves about a specific revision, the Global BBT
Trustees/Directors will be the final arbiter.”

Whereas the BBT, although responsible, feels that input from the GBC is essential in making any
determination about disputes as described, and has requested a set of protocols to deal with this situation.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

Upon the recommendation of the BBT-GBC Relations Committee the following process is adopted by the
GBC Body:
Including, but not limited to, final decisions on the few cases (five cases in the Introduction and 1st
Chapter of Bhagavad-gita) where the ERP and the BBT Editorial Board cannot come to a
consensus, that a committee comprising three qualified BBT members and three qualified GBC
members be formed to be the final arbiter in the case of any dispute between the ERP and the BBT
Editorial Board. The three qualified BBT members will be chosen by the BBT Trustees, and the
three qualified GBC members will be chosen by the GBC body. Once those six members are
chosen, at their first meeting they will discuss and agree on a seventh member and all decisions will
require five of the seven members to vote in favor for it to be ratified.

Footnote:

The GBC have chosen Bhakti Caitanya Swami, Prahladananda Swami and Tapana Misra dasa as their
three members to serve on this committee.

305.06 · Sarasvata Gaudiya Vaisnava Association (2022)

ISKCON related organizations: Sarasvata Gaudiya Vaisnava
[Statement]

Association

Whereas Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura instructed his disciples to work together

Whereas to reunite the Sarasvata Gaudiya family as a primary objective, Srila Prabhupada established the
Bhaktivedanta Swami Charity Trust (BSCT) on the 5th of November 1977, comprised of ISKCON and
Gaudiya Math members

Whereas in or around 1980, the BSCT, subsequently formed the Sarasvata Gaudiya Vaishnava
Association (SGVA) with the blessings of the then present god-brothers of Srila Prabhupada, such as Srila
Bhakti Pramod Puri Maharaja, Srila Bhakti Vaibhava Puri Maharaja, and others

Whereas ISKCON Sri Mayapur has consistently established cordial relations with many neighbouring
Gaudiya Maths and international leaders alike over the past fifty years or more

Whereas many of them have shown interest in becoming part of the SGVA

Whereas under the circumstances, it is prudent to formalize a legal constitution of the SGVA.

Therefore, it is resolved that:
1. The GBC agrees in principle to join the formally incorporated SGVA.

2. Jayapataka Swami, Bhakti Purusottama Swami and Bhadra Balarama dasa are assigned to draft a
constitution for the SVGA in consultation with the various stakeholders.

3. When the constitution is ready, the GBC Body will review it.

4. After reviewing the SGVA constitution the GBC will decide on its participation/membership.

5. If the GBC decides to join the formal SGVA it will assign representatives to attend meetings.

301.05 · Narahari dasa’s Suspension as an Initiating Guru in ISKCON (2023)

ISKCON Members: Individual devotees
[Statement]

Whereas considering that the concerns raised by the Hawaii temple board about Narahari prabhu’s
activities and their opinion that he should not be allowed to resume giving initiations, and considering that
Narahari dasa continues to make aspiring disciples despite the GBC’s and the North American RGB’s
decision that he should not do so

Therefore, it is resolved that:

North American RGB.

Also, during his suspension, Narahari dasa will not canvas, promise initiation or give initiation to anyone
anywhere in the world, including the aspiring disciples that he presently has. He will also inform those who
are now aspiring for initiation that he was not and is not now authorized to accept aspiring disciples.

The North American RGB and the Guru Services Committee will work together to reach any future
decisions concerning Narahari dasa’s suspension.

301.01 · Puspa-samadhis in ISKCON (2025)

ISKCON members: Regulations
[Governing law]

Whereas a clear resolution is required regarding the establishment of puspa-samadhis to avoid conflicting
final instructions;

Whereas with the passage of time, the departure of senior Vaisnavas is becoming more prevalent, creating
an urgency for a concise statement

Therefore, it is resolved that:

No puspa-samadhis will be erected for any member of ISKCON in the future, effective March 19, 2025. Any
senior Vaisnava whose followers choose to erect a samadhi may erect only one samadhi in total after
receiving the approval of the GBC Vaisnava Memorial Standing Committee.

Every ISKCON guru shall include this instruction in their will.

302.05 · Encouraging the establishment and maintenance of ISKCON temple (2025)

Asramas (spiritual orders) in ISKCON: General
[Guideline]

asramas — 2025

Whereas Srila Prabhupada established and built ISKCON upon the strength of temples with vibrant
asramas;

Whereas many if not most ISKCON temples in the West and elsewhere have minimized or closed their
asramas in the course of evolving toward congregational development;

Whereas the current need for finding qualified devotees to take leadership roles in ISKCON can be largely
met by providing asrama training and experience for more young devotees

Therefore, it is resolved that:

The GBC encourages all ISKCON temples who currently do not have active resident asramas to
deliberately and diligently establish or re-establish them according to the following best practices:

1. Though resident asramas may sometimes accommodate older devotees, in general, temples shall
provide asrama accommodation for young people newly taking up Krishna consciousness as a
training ground for their future lives as devotees. At the same time, the contributions and needs of
older devotees, who have dedicated years of their lives to Srila Prabhupada’s movement, are
deeply valued and respected. Temples may also offer facilities to support and integrate older
devotees into the community. To welcome and nurture newcomers, we must provide protected
asrama space for them, while also honoring and accommodating the senior devotees who have laid
the foundation for this spiritual movement. This balanced approach ensures that both older and
younger devotees are cared for and encouraged in their spiritual journeys.

2. Resident asrama schedules should be manageable and moderate so that students have sufficient
time for a balanced life of sadhana, seva, recreation and rest.

3. Initial seva assignments may include menial tasks, but in time leaders should seek to provide
asrama students in varieties of experiences including training in kirtana, instruments, public
speaking and management tasks.

4. Resident asramas should have dedicated leaders who understand the sensitivity of training new
students and whose only service is the well-being of new students.

5. Except in parts of the world where women’s asramas are culturally unacceptable, resident asramas
should provide separate but equal facility for men and women, as per Srila Prabhupada’s
instruction.

6. In addition to equal asrama facility, where culturally appropriate, aspiring Vaisnavis should be given
equal opportunity and encouragement for worship, preaching and service.

7. Courses in Bhakti Sastri and the ISKCON Disciples Course should be provided for asrama students.

8. As nearly all new devotees marry, grhastha training should be part of the curriculum, even for those
who are interested in pursuing renunciation.

307.09 · Honoring the sacred birthplace of Bhaktivinoda Thakura (2025)

ISKCON — other: The sacred birthplace of Bhaktivinoda
[Statement]

Thakura

Whereas Birnagar is the birthplace of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura, and it holds significant historical and
spiritual importance for devotees;

Whereas Srila Prabhupada expressed his deep desire to develop Birnagar to broadcast the glories of Srila
Bhaktivinoda Thakura, the eminent Acarya of this Gaudiya Sampradaya, to the world;

Whereas Srila Prabhupada had a profound desire to honor Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura by developing his
birthplace in Birnagar into a significant center for spiritual education and pilgrimage;

Whereas the Birnagar project is one of the most important projects for every Gaudiya Vaisnava, especially
for our movement;

Whereas Srila Prabhupada requested the Bhaktivinoda Gosthi (the Managing Committee of the Birnagar
Dvadasa Temple), Srila Lalita Prasada Thakura, to permit us to render this service. Unfortunately, however,
he and the committee did not accept the proposal;

Whereas even after 52 years we have not been successful, as the Bhaktivinoda Gosthi still does not agree
to our proposal for developing the Janma-sthana;
Whereas through the Bhaktivedanta Swami Charity Trust some renovations and construction work for the
Birnagar Dvadasa Siva Mandir were carried out. The Birnagar Bhaktivinoda Gosthi is willing to accept the
construction but is not ready to grant us any sevaiteship. If they do not provide sevaiteship, they will be
unable to maintain a large temple on their property after its construction;

Whereas the Bhaktivinoda Gosthi is not ready to give us the land, either on lease or through any other
arrangement as of now;

Whereas, as per the desire of Srila Prabhupada, ISKCON should establish a magnificent temple for
Bhaktivinoda Thakura, along with a display of his life history, his writings, an educational center, parks and
gardens, guesthouses, an asrama, and more;

Whereas ISKCON should purchase land in Birnagar next to Bhaktivinoda Thakura’s birthplace and develop
a memorial and temple for the great Acarya Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura;

Whereas, since this is a big project, it should be directly supported and managed by ISKCON

Therefore, it is resolved that:

To fulfill Srila Prabhupada’s desire and instruction to establish a temple at the birthplace of Srila
Bhaktivinoda Thakura, the GBC will actively support the Birnagar Project Committee in this important
initiative.

The plan includes developing a magnificent temple and other facilities envisioned by Srila Prabhupada near
the birthplace on land free from lease restrictions. A 4.5-acre plot, located just 300 meters from the current
temple, is available, and the committee is working on acquiring it. Simultaneously, the committee will
continue efforts to negotiate with the management of the Birnagar Dvadasa Temple to secure sevaiteship of
the existing birthplace temple.

The GBC empowers the committee to raise awareness within the devotee community about the spiritual
significance of this project, inspiring devotees to actively participate in its service and contribute to its
successful development.

Any fundraising efforts must be approved in advance in writing by local and regional ISKCON leadership.

301.09 · Notice of Censure of Kamalesh Krishna dasa, Lilasuka devi dasi and (2026)

ISKCON members: Letters of censure
[Statement]

Daksina devi dasi —2026

Resolved that:

The GBC issues the following letter of censure:

Dear Kamalesh Krishna Prabhu,

Please accept our humble obeisances. All glories to Srila Prabhupada.

This letter records the formal censure adopted by the Governing Body Commission (GBC) in
respect of yourself for non-compliance with GBC Resolution 450.03, passed on 21 February 2025.

As you are aware, the GBC approved an Enhanced Child Protection Model on 3 January 2025.
Shortly thereafter, the newly established GBC Standing Committee — Child Protection Oversight
Committee (CPOC)—formally requested the handover of website and email credentials as early as
11 January 2025, followed by additional requests for key documentation. Multiple emails were sent
inviting you to attend a meeting to facilitate a structured transition, but no agreement was received,
and the meeting never took place.
Subsequently, a Resolution 450.03 issued on 21 February 2025 required that the Minister of Justice
serve as transitional ICPO Director and specifically asked for a comprehensive handover to be
conducted by you, Kamalesh Krishna dasa, as the outgoing ICPO Director by the 1st of March 2025.
The resolution referred to the handover, inter alia, the transfer of case file notes, status reports,
incomplete case materials, investigator and panelist contact information, and all relevant databases
and records necessary to ensure continuity of safeguarding oversight. The resolution is clear and
binding.

The required comprehensive handover has, as of 9th February 2026 being the date of the issuing of
this censure, not occurred.

Over the past year, the matter was addressed with you via CPOC, ISKCON’s General Counsel and
the GBC Executive Committee. Additionally, a GBC EC File Note was issued in June 2025. When
compliance was still not forthcoming, the GBC EC issued a final letter of demand dated 24
November 2025 to you and Lilasuka devi dasi. A response was submitted by yourself on the final
day of the deadline, 15 December 2025, wherein you changed your stance from not having the
files/access to the files to an assertion that legal restrictions prevented transfer, a concern that had
never previously been raised and that, if valid, could have been addressed at the time the handover
was required.

As a result thereof an external legal opinion was sought by the GBC’s General Counsel which
determined that you, as the former ICPO Director acted under GBC authority as an agent of
ISKCON, that the records constitute ISKCON proprietary information, and that refusal to transfer
them to the GBC’s authorized representative is not legally justified.

This conclusion reflects not only the legal position, but also the most basic standards of institutional
common sense and leadership accountability. Your continued withholding of these records for
almost one year has impeded the implementation of the GBC-approved child protection framework
and has disrupted continuity of oversight in a safeguarding context.

Daksina devi dasi who had resigned as the UK CPO director, continued to upload case files on
behalf of your defunct office and serve in the North American CPO during Lilasuka devi dasi’s
medical leave period, having full access to all file data. Notably, Lilasuka devi dasi and Daksina devi
dasi, who were fully aware of the transference directive and had the means to facilitate it, likewise
failed and/or refused to act.

These failures reveal not isolated mistakes, but a systemic lack of stewardship, supervision, and
commitment to institutional continuity. This reflects a chain of defiance and accountability lapses at
the highest level as compliance with duly adopted GBC resolutions is an essential obligation of
service within ISKCON, while the transfer of institutional records during authorized transitions is
necessary to maintain continuity, accountability, and the protection of those served.

Accordingly, the GBC formally censures:

You, Kamalesh Krishna dasa, for failure to execute the comprehensive handover mandated by
Resolution 450.03 and failure to exercise basic foresight and leadership.

Lilasuka devi dasi and Daksina devi dasi, for facilitating or supporting the continued withholding of
CPO files and databases, in circumstances where transference could have been facilitated by them.
It is to be noted that after the November 2025 demand, Lilasuka devi dasi transferred only seven
case files to ISKCON’s General Counsel. These seven files relate only to open North American
cases. She continues to retain possession of all remaining ISKCON Child Protection files, both hard
and soft copies.

The GBC regards this non-compliance as a serious failure in the discharge of institutional
responsibility and considers it a severe case of incompetence and negligence. Such conduct is
inconsistent with the standards expected of those entrusted with governance and safeguarding
responsibilities, and is incompatible with any role requiring trust, accountability, and prudent
judgment. Given the fact that you had a fiduciary responsibility—timing, delegation, and inherited
arrangements do not excuse the absence of decisive leadership at a critical transition point as
delegation of tasks does not equal delegation of responsibility. Safeguarding documentations
represent the core operational responsibility of the office, and securing its orderly transfer should
have been an intentional, proactive act of stewardship. The situation reflects not merely an
administrative oversight, but a concerning lack of foresight, ownership, and leadership judgment at
the close of your mandate.

Accordingly, your conduct, particularly your non-compliance with a duly adopted GBC resolution,
reflects a serious departure from the standards of cooperation and accountability expected of those
entrusted with the protection of children and holding office in ISKCON. This has resulted in a loss of
institutional confidence and raises serious concerns regarding suitability for future engagement in
any office or position within ISKCON involving leadership, governance authority, oversight functions,
institutional records, or child protection responsibilities.

On behalf of the GBC Body,

Your servants,

Govardhana Das
Tapana Misra Das
Madhu Sevita Das,
(GBC Executive Committee)

303.04 · Sale of the ISKCON Wellington property — 2025 (2026)

ISKCON — centers and affiliates: Individual centers
[Action order]

Whereas the GBC Executors Property Oversight Committee (GEPOC) recommends approving the sale of
the Wellington, NZ, temple based on use of all net sale proceeds for purchasing a new, larger, code-
compliant temple building, for the following reasons:

1. The current Wellington, NZ temple was ordered closed for public assembly unless it is renovated to
meet building codes and specifically handicap accessibility. That would entail rebuilding or adding
handicap accessible bathrooms. Currently the temple cannot be used for public worship, kirtan,
classes or serving prasadam to devotees and guests.

2. If such renovations were performed, then the local authorities could apply for zoning for public
assembly, etc.

3. If such renovations were to be planned, it was felt by local GBC and the temple president that the
entire building should be raised to avoid the regular flooding that occurs during heavy rains.

4. The local GBC and temple president feel that even if such costly renovation work were performed,
the temple doesn’t allow for growth, or even for safe parking.

5. The local GBC and temple president have identified an alternate building in Petone (20 miles away)
which is for sale, which is code compliant with adequate parking, currently used for commercial
offices. If purchased, a renovation can be performed to create a large temple room suitable for the
deities and suitable to accommodate a growing devotee and life member community.

6. The temple president has raised and banked in an ISKCON account almost $700,000 NZD for the
purchase. The sale proceeds from the current Wellington site would bring in sufficient additional
funds to complete the purchase, albeit with a larger mortgage than currently exists on the
Wellington temple property.
7. The current deities are relatively small Gaura Nitai deities, which can be safely moved. The
ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry has stated no objection to the move, based on obtaining Hutt City
Council zoning for temple/public assembly.

Whereas based on the above reasons, GEPOC has no objection to the proposed sale for the stated
purpose

Therefore, it is resolved that:

The GBC hereby approves of the sale of the ISKCON Wellington property as presented.

2 Srila Prabhupada, the Founder-Acarya of ISKCON

2.1 Definition

To fulfill the previous acarya's desire for a united worldwide preaching organization to expand Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu's mission, Srila Prabhupada founded the International Society for Krishna Consciousness as a distinct branch of the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya-Vaisnava-sampradaya. Therefore he is the Founder-Acarya of ISKCON.

His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada is the Founder-Acarya of ISKCON. This means that he is ISKCON's link with the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya sampradaya, that his writings, oral teachings, and exemplary actions remain the permanent and irreplaceable basis for all subsequent teachings and activities of ISKCON. He is and will remain always the instructing spiritual master of all devotees in ISKCON. (Law Revision committee 9.6.90)

2.2 Principles

2.2.1 The Significance of Srila Prabhupada to ISKCON

1. Srila Prabhupada is the foundational siksa-guru for all ISKCON devotees because he has realized and presented the teachings of the previous acaryas of the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya-sampradaya appropriately for the modern age.

2. Srila Prabhupada's instructions are the essential teachings for every ISKCON devotee.

3. Srila Prabhupada's books are the embodiment of his teachings and should be accepted as the standard by all future generations of ISKCON.

4. Srila Prabhupada should be worshipped daily by every ISKCON member.

5. Every ISKCON spiritual master is responsible to guide his disciples to follow Srila Prabhupada's instructions.

6. As Founder-Acarya, Srila Prabhupada gave directions for management, principles of cooperation, and other practical guidelines which form the basis and inspiration for ISKCON's policies.

7. Srila Prabhupada established the Governing Body Commission to execute his will, following the order of the previous acaryas.(94)

2.2.2 Recognition of Srila Prabhupada's Position as the Founder-Acarya of ISKCON

The position of Srila Prabhupada as Founder-Acarya shall be recognized in ISKCON through the use of the titles "Founder-Acarya," "Founder," and "Prabhupada," and through the establishment of shrines in places of Srila Prabhupada's pastimes, memorials and plaques to his memory.

2.3 Regulations

2.3.1 Use of Title

1. The titles "Founder-Acarya," "Founder," and "Prabhupada" can be used only in reference to His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada. Srila Prabhupada's full name shall be displayed along with his titles "Founder-Acarya" and "Prabhupada" on all printed materials, signs, letterheads, and in connection with all ISKCON projects.(83)

2. The title "Prabhupada" should be included on all printed materials, signs, etc. and only be used for Srila Prabhupada.(83)

3. All ISKCON publications such as books, magazines, newsletters, leaflets, fliers, invitations, etc., should clearly display the full name and titles of Srila Prabhupada including Founder-Acarya, Prabhupada, and His Divine Grace, for example:

"His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada,

Founder-Acarya of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness".(96)

2.3.2 Shrines and Memorials

1. Places of Srila Prabhupada's pastimes shall be maintained as permanent shrines, and his paraphernalia shall be collected and preserved in memorials to him.

2. The responsibility for maintaining the worship of Srila Prabhupada shall be borne by ISKCON as a whole and distributed among the temples and initiated devotees of the Society.

3. There shall be a committee named "The Bhaktivedanta Swami Memorial Committee" whose members are appointed by the GBC. It will determine where and how Srila Prabhupada's rooms and paraphernalia shall be preserved.

Srila Prabhupada's rooms in the following places shall be maintained as permanent shrines in remembrance of his pastimes:

1. Vrndavana-dhama

2. Mayapur-dhama

3. Bombay

4. Los Angeles

5. Honolulu

6. Atlanta

7. Detroit

Srila Prabhupada's original grass hut (Bhajana Kutira) at Sri Mayapur shall be a Bhaktivedanta Swami memorial shrine.(81)

The Sannyasa Ministry and the Vrndavana Temple Management shall take joint responsibility for maintaining the worship in Srila Prabhupada's rooms at Radha-Damodara temple.(90)

2.3.2.1 Samadhi Mandirs at Sri Vrndavana-dhama and Sri Mayapur-dhama

ISKCON shall establish and perpetually maintain worship of Srila Prabhupada in his Samadhi Mandir at Sri Vrndavana-dhama and his Puspa-Samadhi Mandir at Sri Mayapur-dhama.

Temples or zones shall pledge to maintain the worship of Srila Prabhupada's Samadhi in Vrndavana according to the established system.
