429.2 · Law Book — Categories (2019)

Law Book Committee
[Rule of order]

(Proposed by Nrsimha Kavaca Das and Sponsored by Madhu Sevita Das and Praghosa Das)
Whereas the categories use to classify resolutions passed by the GBC have evolved over time, as
can be seen by the following:
1987:
1997:
All resolutions be categorized as a rule of order, law, or provisional order at the time of
passing.
That all GBC resolutions shall be categorized as one of the following:
a. Action Order (administrative, appointment, action oriented, directive or provisional
orders, plus send to or form a committee, etc. that is temporary in nature and expires on
completion)
b. GBC Rule of Order (permanent in nature)
c. ISKCON Law (permanent in nature)
d. ISKCON Vision and Goal (time bound) (future planning, strategies, standing objectives
which push on the preaching of the Society and position papers, statements of
appreciation, etc. that are permanent in nature), and
e. Guideline (behavior or action for ISKCON).
2010:
The following terms, when used as descriptions of the intent of GBC Resolutions and
included in the language of the resolution when passed by the Body, shall henceforward
have the following meanings:
1. LAW: A statement of principle applicable permanently to the whole of ISKCON.
1. GUIDELINE: A statement of principle recommended to be adopted by the whole
of ISKCON.
2. RULE OF ORDER: A rule governing the internal functioning of the GBC Body.
The Rules of Order as a whole also form a default set of rules for the internal
functioning of other ISKCON administrative bodies, to be followed as applicable
to their various circumstances, unless the other body has specifically resolved
that it shall function differently.
Laws, Guidelines, and Rules of Order, in order to have the effect of Laws, Guidelines,
and Rules of Order as described in these definitions, must be declared as such within
the language of the resolution when passed by the GBC Body. The GBC Executive
Committee shall cause updated compilations of all current Laws, Guidelines, and Rules
of Order to be maintained and regularly made available to the society.
Other declarations of categories shall be optional, and the intent of a resolution shall be
determined by the wording of the resolution itself and not by the category declared.
Whereas the existing categorizations of GBC resolutions have been found to be inadequate, and to
some degree inappropriate, for the present functioning of the GBC;
Whereas the intent of the above resolutions – to help minimize confusion and improve the resolutions’
usability – was partly accomplished, it has been found that not all resolutions fit neatly into one of
these categories, and some mis-categorizations have increased confusion rather than reducing it;
Whereas a better policy will be to let the resolution speak for itself, with optional categorization
included in the resolution wording when such is deemed helpful to convey the intent of the resolution;
Whereas for those resolutions that establish enduring principles, the GBC should provide standard
definitions for the category terms;
Whereas the GBC directed the current ISKCON Law Book Committee to keep as much of the work of
the previous committee as possible, and;
Whereas the following was unanimously passed by the GBC at the AGM in 2016 but not recorded.
Resolved:
The following categories must be used to define any proposal being presented to the GBC Body to
describe the intent of the proposal.
This language which will be included in the final resolution shall henceforward have the following
meanings:
1. Constitutional principles
Enduring principles based on Prabhupada's teachings on how ISKCON should be
organized.
Enduring features of ISKCON as per Prabhupada's teachings.
2. Governing laws:
Rules governing the practical functioning of ISKCON which are globally applicable.
3. Statutory regulations:
The Memorandum and Articles of Association which govern the internal functioning of
the ISKCON GBC Society West Bengal.
4. Rules of order:
Procedures for the functioning of the GBC Body.
5. Administrative guidelines:
Detailed description of the practical application of laws. Includes Administrative Orders,
Action Orders, Position Papers and Statements.
a. Administrative order:
Orders by which an administrative wing or branch of ISKCON with specific functions is
created. E.g. a ministry or other functional unit that has an existence beyond the scope
of the individuals performing the task.
b. Action order
A directive to a specific individual or group of individuals to perform a time bound task.
c. Position statements
Considered conclusions of the Body on particular subject matters.
d. Statements
Declarations setting forth decisions of the Body.
e. Guidelines
Guidance relative to setting standards or determining a course of action.
f. Votes of thanks
Statements of appreciation or recognition of outstanding service or contributions to
ISKCON.

429.2 · Law Book — One Category per Resolution (2019)

Law Book Committee
[Rule of order]

(Proposed by Nrsimha Kavaca Das and sponsored by Madhu Sevita Das and Praghosa Das)
Whereas the current Law Book Committee has been working to make the body of GBC resolutions
more accessible to the members of ISKCON;
Whereas this has resulted in the development of a web-based database;
Whereas in order to focus the search feature of the database the search criteria must be very
specific;
Whereas resolutions that have more than one category are more difficult to enter and refine the
search.
Resolved:
All proposals shall only include one category as defined in the above resolution “Lawbook —
Categories — 2019.”
For proposal concepts that require more than one category, e.g. “Action order,” “ISKCON law,” etc.,
each section requiring its own category must be presented as a separate proposal.

429.2 · Law Book — Content Layout (2019)

Law Book Committee
[Rule of order]

(Proposed by Nrsimha Kavaca Das and Sponsored by Madhu Sevita Das and Praghosa Das)
Whereas entering data into the Law Book Database is very time consuming and will be greatly
simplified if the content and structure of proposals and resolutions match the database data entry
fields;
Whereas there are many resolutions that have titles that do not assist the user in understanding the
content of the resolution, such as in 2001 a proposal was submitted named, “Show cause notice”.
The proposal was actually informing the GBC that a show cause notice relating to Adridharan Das
was pending before the high court. This is not apparent from the title.
Whereas crafting ISKCON legislation is often a very detailed and time-consuming task and if
ISKCON’s legislators have sufficient information on hand they will gain a deeper understanding of the
thought process and background that led to such resolutions being drafted and passed;
Resolved:
All proposals and resolutions must include the following data fields in the order as listed below:
Section
Title
Year
Meeting
Category
Presentation of proposal
Resolution
Tags
Published
Amendment
Proposed by
Sponsored by
Footnotes to resolution
Explanatory notes:
Section — according to “Sections used to sort resolutions — 2019”
Title must also include the year it was passed. This will facilitate finding relevant resolutions.
Year — year resolution passed
Presentation of proposal — where applicable, all proposals should include.
Resolution
Tags — this will enable search feature.
Published — is this resolution to be published or unpublished.
Amendment — is this an amendment to another resolution. Identify other resolution.
Proposed by — name of proposer(s)
Sponsored by — name of sponsors
Footnotes to resolution — any footnotes to resolution

407.02 · Amendment to Certificate of Readiness—Appeal process (2020)

ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry (IDWM)

Governing law
Whereas ISKCON Governing Law 407.02, “Regulation of Deity installations — 2012” does not include any
information directing centers how to appeal decisions by the ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry
Whereas ISKCON centers have the right to appeal a decision
Whereas ISKCON centers should understand the process for appealing a decision
And whereas there is already an existing appeal process in ISKCON Law
RESOLVED:
ISKCON law 407.02, “Regulation of Deity installations — 2012” for commencing worship of Deities in
ISKCON is amended to include the following:
Any ISKCON center that has applied to the ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry for a Certificate of
Readiness to commence worship of deities, but their application has not been successful, may appeal
the decision via the following process:
1. Communicate to the ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry that they are not satisfied with the
decision.
http://deityworship.com/
10
2. IDWM will then offer a written explanation of the decision.
3. If the center is still not satisfied with the outcome of that communication then they have the
option to follow the appeals process established by GBC resolution 604.2, Appeal of Decisions
to GBC Executive Committee 2005.
The full revised law is below:
Any ISKCON center wishing to install any deities for public temple worship or commence the worship of
any deity in an ISKCON center must first receive a “Certificate of Readiness for Worship” for the said
deities.
Centers may procure deities and begin promoting planned temple openings or additions to existing worship
once they have successfully completed the first stage of the approval process. Centers shall not commit to
and/or publicly advertise final dates for commencement of worship until they receive a “Certificate of
Readiness for Worship.”
This “Certificate of Readiness for Worship” applies only to the deities for which it is granted and is not a
generic permanent approval.
The initial contact: The center wishing to commence the worship of deities makes an application via the
ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry’s website, Deityworship.com. After receiving this application, the IDWM
contacts the local GBC and regional authorities to assess the viability of the application. If this consultation
shows the center has made a proper analysis of the requirements to worship deities and are moving in the
right direction regarding allocation, resources, etc. to the worship of the deities then the first stage approval
is granted. This then enables the temple to make arrangements to acquire deities and commence fund-
raising, etc.
The second and final stage will be assessed based on the findings of a site visit by an IDWM
representative, or comprehensive consultation with concerned devotees.
The readiness for worship will be assessed by a local representative (from the temple concerned); the local
GBC, regional leadership (which may include a representative from the National Council or RGB, etc.); and
an ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry representative. The GBC Executive Committee will be informed of the
assessment outcome.
For any applications for deities apart from those given by Srila Prabhupada, i.e. Radha-Krsna; Jagannatha,
Baladeva, Subhadra; and Gaura-Nitai (or Panca-tattva) and salagram silas, the IDWM requires executive
input.
Therefore, for any application that includes Krsna-Balarama or Sita Rama Lakshman Hanuman, the IDWM
will consult with the GBC Executive Committee for approval.
Any deities apart from the aforementioned must be approved by the GBC Body before the IDWM can issue
a Certificate of Readiness for installing deities.
This Certificate of Readiness is valid for up to 180 days beyond the initial scheduled installation date. If the
180-day period has elapsed without the installation being completed, the temple will be reassessed by the
ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry for a new Certificate of Readiness to be issued.
Any ISKCON center that has applied to the ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry for a Certificate of Readiness
to commence worship of Deities, but their application has not been successful, may appeal the decision via
the following process:
1. Communicate to the ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry that they are not satisfied with the decision.
2. IDWM will then offer a written explanation of the decision.
3. If the center is still not satisfied with the outcome of that communication then they have the option to
follow the appeals process established by GBC resolution 604.2, Appeal of Decisions to GBC
Executive Committee 2005.
11

423.03 · In-depth study of variations in second initiation policies (2020)

Guru Services Committee

Action order
Whereas different initiating gurus in ISKCON have established different policies regarding when second
initiation may be offered to an ISKCON member. Some offer second initiation quite readily to all, regardless
of the service they are performing in the society, and others offer second initiation readily only to those who
are expected to be engaged in worship of ISKCON temple deities, and very few others
Whereas the Board of Examinations has established a standard for admission of a candidate for a
Bhaktivedanta degree program whereby second initiation is a prerequisite for enrolment, and it will soon be
publishing a revised standard for this degree that removes this prerequisite, but adds the requirement that
the candidate must be second-initiated in order to actually receive a Bhaktivedanta degree
Whereas this lack of uniformity in second initiation policies of ISKCON's initiating gurus may be the source
of unnecessary conflict and confusion
Whereas some ISKCON gurus have changed Srila Prabhupada’s requirements for second initiation
RESOLVED:
That the Guru Services Committee is directed to arrange for an in-depth study of the varying policies for
second initiation and present their recommendations to the GBC at the 2021 AGM.

409.01 · Mood of worship (2021)

ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry: Standards
[Statement]

Whereas deity worship is an essential element of the process of bhakti and the development of a sadhaka;

Whereas it is intrinsic to a devotee’s development in bhakti, and when engaged in deity worship, that a
devotee follows the proper rules and regulations governing the worship and understand and follow the
appropriate mood of worship;

Whereas devotees who have not attained the platform of spontaneous attachment in devotional service
render devotional service under the guidance of a bona fide spiritual master according to the regulative
principles mentioned in the revealed scriptures;

Whereas Lord Caitanya explained the mood of worship to Sanatana Goswami as awe and reverence:

sadhu-sanga, nama-kirtana, bhagavata-sravana
mathura-vasa, sri-murtira sraddhaya sevana

13
One should associate with devotees, chant the holy name of the Lord, hear Srimad-
Bhagavatam, reside at Mathura and worship the Deity with faith and veneration. CC Madhya
22.128

Whereas Srila Prabhupada in his books and other writings, has established the mood of worship for
ISKCON temples, most notably in SB 4.24.45-46:

Generally the worship of the Lord begins with the worship of Narayana, or Visnu, whereas the
worship of Lord Krsna and Radha is most confidential. Lord Narayana is worshipable by the
pancaratrika-vidhi, or regulative principles, whereas Lord Krsna is worshipable by the bhagavata-
vidhi. No one can worship the Lord in the bhagavata-vidhi without going through the regulations of
the pancaratrika-vidhi. Actually, neophyte devotees worship the Lord according to the pancaratrika-
vidhi, or the regulative principles enjoined in the Narada Pancaratra. Radha-Krsna cannot be
approached by the neophyte devotees; therefore temple worship according to regulative principles
is offered to Laksmi-Narayana. Although there may be a Radha-Krsna vigraha, or form, the worship
of the neophyte devotees is acceptable as Laksmi-Narayana worship. Worship according to the
pancaratrika-vidhi is called vidhi-marga, and worship according to the bhagavata-vidhi principles is
called raga-marga. The principles of raga-marga are especially meant for devotees who are
elevated to the Vrndavana platform.

Whereas Srila Prabhupada has explained: The greatest danger to our movement will come when we
manufacture and create our own process for worshiping the deities. Letter Jan. 4, 1973;

Whereas deity worship is not a forum for free expression where devotees are able to offer service
according to their own idea, but it must be offered according to the direction of guru, sadhu, and sastra;

Whereas Srila Prabhupada established specific standards of deity worship in ISKCON with the mood of
awe and reverence being the most central to these standards;

Whereas in recent years we have noticed a steady drift away from this mood of worship established by
Srila Prabhupada;

Whereas it is apparent in various temples that this mood of worship is not being followed or has not been
understood.

RESOLVED:
The GBC reaffirms that the mood of worship established by Srila Prabhupada, which is to be followed in all
ISKCON centres, is the mood of awe and reverence.

All worship conducted in ISKCON centres, both regular daily worship and occasional worship (such as
festivals), must be conducted according to this standard.

All ISKCON leaders are required to ensure that devotees and centres under their care understand and
implement worship according to these standards.

As such, all practices that demonstrate a different mood of worship are not approved and must be actively
discouraged by leaders at all levels. This includes but is not limited to:
• Devotees’ conduct in the presence of the deities
• The way devotees interact with the deities
• The manner in which devotees dress the deities, and
• The different aspects of daily and festival services

440.01 · Establishing the Vaisnava Memorial Standing Committee [VMSC] (2021)

[Administrative order]

Establishing the committee

Whereas the GBC affirms there is a need to have standard policy on the establishment of Vaisnava
memorials and who is eligible for what type of memorial;

Whereas the GBC deems this is a task that should be overseen by a committee and therefore, at the 2008
AGM, passed the following Resolution:

That the standing Commemoration Committee is established with the mandate as follows:
1. To research and establish a standard set of guidelines documenting the process for correctly
honoring departed Vaisnavas.
2. To maintain records of departed ISKCON Vaisnavas and a summary of their services for the
society.
3. To determine the application of the guidelines in individual cases.
4. To decide which of the departed disciples of Srila Prabhupada will be interred in full, given a
puspa samadhi, or honored with a plaque in the Mayapur Garden of Inspiration.
Praghosa dasa (convenor), Bhakti Caru Swami, Bhakti Purusottama Swami, and Mahamaya devi
dasi are assigned to the standing committee.

Whereas this committee was never active;

Whereas the committee's focus is to establish guidelines for, and approval for Vaisnavas who may be
remembered in memorial parks, Vaisnava Memorial Standing Committee (VMSC), is a more appropriate
name;

Whereas, as the devotee population ages, an increasing number of devotees are passing away and the
need to establish a universal policy for Vaisnava memorials is ever more pressing.

RESOLVED:
That the GBC re-establishes the Commemoration Standing Committee and renames it the Vaisnava
Memorial Standing Committee. The mandate or scope of the Vaisnava Memorial Standing Committee will
be as follows:

15
1. To research and establish a standard, global policy for appropriately honoring departed devotees.
Such a policy will take into account, and reflect the global diversity of ISKCON, and shall duly
respect the contribution of Vaisnavas as well as Vaisnavis.

2. To proactively reach out to all sannyasis, gurus, GBCs and other senior devotees to establish what
they want done with their bodies or remains after their passing away, either by obtaining a copy of
their will and testament, or by their own written statement, and:

a. Establish and maintain a list of devotees who are eligible for samadhi, either full body or
other;
b. Decide how departed devotees will be honored;
c. Determine what standard size of memorial is appropriate for all departed devotees;
d. Identify exceptional cases and refer them to the GBC body.

3. To communicate with regional bodies and temples, looking for recommendations for candidates for
samadhi.

4. To maintain records of departed devotees and a summary of their services for ISKCON, and to
make this information readily available to the members of ISKCON, through a website, and/or other
suitable means.

440.02 · Samadhis for Sannyasis — 2020 (2021)

Vaisnava Memorial Standing Committee (VMSC)
[Statement]

Regulations

16
Whereas the GBC Samadhi Committee has presented evidence that sannyasis are generally buried;

Whereas it is not essential that a ‘samadhi structure’ be erected over the body of a departed sannyasi.
Instead a tulasi plant or a tree could be planted over their body;

Whereas of the 21 GBC members that voted on the question “Should Sannyasis automatically get a vapu
samadhi?” 16 voted against;

Whereas of the 45 sannyasis that responded to a SABHA survey on samadhis, 22 said they did not want
their bodies put in samadhi;

Whereas Srila Prabhupada said ‘Anyone who is in full Krishna Consciousness and is dedicating his life for
Krishna is already a sannyasi even if he is a married man.’

RESOLVED:
That although sannyasis are usually buried, it is not essential this must be done nor is it essential that a
samadhi structure be erected for every sannyasi.

17

Prabhupada, and the guru parampara;

440.02 · Worship at Vaiṣṇava samadhis — 2020 (2021)

Vaisnava Memorial Standing Committee (VMSC)
[Statement]

Regulations

Whereas at present there is daily worship going on at Srila Prabhupada’s Puspa Samadhi;

Whereas the worship at other existing samadhis is going on at different levels depending on the disciples of
the devotee(s) involved;

Whereas of the 21 GBC members that voted in the survey, 13 GBC members opted for no daily worship at
the individual samadhis;

Whereas ISKCON Law 701.05, “Guru Worship Standards —2009” amends ISKCON Law 6.4.8.1.3 to the
following:

D. In order to focus more fully on Srila Prabhupada and every devotee's special relationship with
him, an ISKCON siksa or diksa guru may accept public guru puja (arati and/or foot bathing) in
person once a year on ISKCON property on his or her Vyasa-puja.

RESOLVED:
1. No daily worship, either individual or collective, is required to be offered to any Vaiṣṇava in any
Vaiṣṇava Memorial Park in Mayapur. However, individuals may occasionally offer incense, flowers,
or prasadam remnants.
18
2. A modest ceremony honoring a departed Vaiṣṇava may be organized on the appearance and
disappearance days of the departed Vaisnava. This function may include offering bhoga, arati,
puspanjali, glorification of the departed Vaiṣṇava, and a feast.

3. In accordance with existing ISKCON Law there will be no murti (deity) of any departed Vaiṣṇava.
There may be a photo of the departed Vaiṣṇava and where applicable a pair of shoes or other
similar paraphernalia.

4. This resolution is retroactive and applies to all existing samadhis located anywhere on ISKCON land
in Mayapur.

ADDED · 2022

406.01 · Amendment to the Minimum Cow Protection Standards: IMCPA (2022)

Ministry of Cow Protection and Agriculture: Regulations
[Statement]

Consultation Team — 2022

Whereas the Minimum Cow Protection Standards established by the ISKCON Ministry for Cow Protection
and Agriculture (IMCPA) in 1999 allows for amendments

Whereas the Standards are intended to guide and regulate practices of cow protection and regenerative
agriculture in ISKCON

Whereas the IMCPA has identified amendments to the current law that will help in educating stakeholders
and resolving issues.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

That the name and functioning of the IMCPA Investigation Team (IT) referred to in the current Minimum
Cow Protection and Agricultural Standards will be changed to the IMCPA Consultation Team (CT) as
shown below:

XV. CONSULTATION TEAM (CT)

Recommended

1. Selection of CT
The Ministry will collect a worldwide list of representatives and consultants to act as a resource pool.
Such devotees will be knowledgeable of the standards and have agricultural experience. From this
list, the Ministry will select an appropriate CT.

2. Travel
To defray travel expenses, representatives who live closest and have knowledge about the problem
in question will be chosen first. Centers receiving the consultants are requested to provide travel
expenses. A fund can eventually be set up to help with travel expenses.

3. Membership of CT
The IMCPA CT should consist of 2 or more devotees not involved in the management of the
program being attended and a professional suited to the situation selected by the CT. The
professional should not be currently employed by the farm receiving the consultancy.

4. Duties of CT
The CT will arrange for group meetings and individual interviews with the stakeholders concerned
and is responsible for the compilation of reports are given to all GBC concerned (Local
Commissioner, Global Secretary, and Cow Protection Ministry).

ADDED · 2022

406.01 · Amendment to law 406.01 Cow Protection Certificate of Readiness (2022)

Ministry of Cow Protection and Agriculture: Regulations
[Governing law]

Whereas to ascertain which projects need to apply for a certificate of readiness, all ISKCON farms and
goshalas must be registered in the ISKCON Ministry of Cow Protection and Agriculture (IMCPA) directory

Whereas the certificate of readiness is a tool to assist with the long-term sustainability of each cow
protection project

Whereas all the major ISKCON farms and goshalas are registered in the directory

Whereas there are still some projects not registered with the directory.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

ISKCON law 406.01 is amended with the following inclusion:

All ISKCON farms and goshalas must be registered in the IMCPA directory. Any project not
registered in the directory by the 30th of March 2023, will have to submit a certificate of readiness to
be registered in the directory.

Existing farms need to be registered with the IMCPA if they are managed by ISKCON even if they
are in the name of a Trust or other entity. The Zonal Supervisors and Zonal Secretaries are
responsible to see that all goshalas and farms are duly registered.

Footnote:

Current law with amendment inserted:

In order to start a cow protection project that will be accredited within ISKCON and accepted as an
ISKCON supported project, a “Cow protection Certificate of Readiness” needs to be obtained.

All ISKCON farms and goshalas must be registered in the IMCPA directory. Any project not registered in
the directory by the 30th of March 2023, will have to submit a certificate of readiness before registration in
the directory.

Existing farms need to be registered with the IMCPA if they are managed by ISKCON even if they are in
the name of a Trust or other entity. The Zonal Supervisors and Zonal Secretaries are responsible to see
that all goshalas and farms are duly registered.

The following are the requirements for obtaining such a certificate, which will allow new cow protection
projects to commence their operations:
The GBC Minimum cow protection standards “ISKCON law 507 (Care for cows — 1999”) needs to be read
and fully understood before applying for the certificate.

An exam must be taken and passed. The questions in the exam will be based on the content of Law 507.

A well-thought-out business plan with the signature of the GBC member must be presented to the Ministry
of Cow Protection and Agriculture.

Details regarding the content that must be addressed in the business plan are provided below in order to
assist in its preparation.

Centers may not make any commitments or agreements regarding procuring and/or acquiring cows until
the “Cow Protection Certificate of Readiness” is granted. The “Certificate of Readiness” applies only to an
ISKCON registered property to which it is granted and is not a generic permanent approval.

The Certificate of Readiness is valid for up to 180 days beyond the initial scheduled acquisition date. If the
180-day period has elapsed without the set up being completed, the center will be reassessed by the
ISKCON Ministry for Cow protection and Agriculture for a new Certificate of Readiness to be issued.

The Cow protection Certificate of Readiness will be assessed by a local representative (from the temple
concerned); the local GBC, regional leadership (which may include a representative from the National
Council or RGB, etc.); and an ISKCON Cow protection and Agriculture (IMCPA) accredited representative.
The GBC Executive Committee will be informed of the assessment outcome.

The initial contact:

The centre wanting to commence a cow protection program makes an application via IMCPA’s website.
After receiving this application which includes a business plan signed by the local GBC, IMCPA contacts
local GBC and regional authorities to assess the viability of the application by their business plan and test.
If process shows the centre has made a proper analysis of requirements for cow protection which includes
agriculture and is moving in the right direction regarding the proper allocation resources, etc. for cow
protection, then the first stage approval is given. This then enables the temple to make arrangements to
acquire cows and commence fund-raising, etc.

The second and final stage will be assessed based on the findings of a site visit by an IMCPA accredited
representative, or comprehensive consultation with concerned devotees.

GBC Resolution 406.02 · 2022 · Online AGM (passed via GEM on August 18, 2022)
Source: resolutions-2022.md | 2022
ADDED · 2022

406.02 · Amendment to Minimum Cow Protection Standards: Pesticides, GMOs, (2022)

Ministry of Cow Protection and Agriculture: Minimum cow
[Governing Law]

protection and agricultural standards
and fertilizers — 2022

Whereas scholars agree that “diverse pesticides directly or indirectly pollute the air, water, soil, and overall
ecosystem which cause a serious health hazard for living beings.” (Sharma et al., 2019)

Whereas the WHO (World Health Organization) and FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization) affirm that
the harmful side-effects of pesticides are becoming increasingly clear. (Global situation of pesticide
management in agriculture and public health, 2021)

Whereas WHO classifies pesticides as carcinogenic (can cause cancer), and neurotoxic (can cause
damage to the brain). (Food safety: Pesticide residue, 2021)

Whereas in places where more than 80 percent of the land is used for industrial agriculture, water tables
are dropping quickly

Whereas Srila Prabhupada spoke profusely on the harm such ugra-karmic technologies bring to the planet,
the environment, public health, the economy, and to human civilization

Whereas Minimum Cow protection standards referenced in ISKCON Law “Care for Cows — 1999,” Section
1, VIII, recommends that “any property (land and cows) belonging to the deity should be protected by
environmentally sound conservation practices designed with the long-term fertility and preservation of the
soil in mind” but does not specify the agricultural standards to accomplish this

Whereas ISKCON has established the minimal cow protection standards but has not yet devised the
standards for agriculture.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

The following agricultural standards will be added to the Minimum Cow Protection and Agricultural
Standards.

The use of:
1. Synthetic pesticides
2. Genetically modified organisms (GMOs)
3. Synthetic fertilizers
will not be allowed in ISKCON projects.

A project may continue to use synthetic fertilizers, at most until 2025, under the condition that they present
a short-term transition plan towards regenerative agriculture.

Regenerative agriculture and agroecology practices are recommended. Organic Agriculture practices are
allowed.

Glossary:
GMO: An organism produced through genetic modification.
Agricultural Biotechnology Glossary https://www.usda.gov/topics/biotechnology/biotechnology-
glossary
Regenerative Agriculture: A holistic, principles-based approach to farming. It seeks to strengthen
soil fertility, community, and water-sources resilience. Such systems include biodynamics,
permaculture design, rotational grazing, biomimicry, agroforestry, syntropic farming, etc. Adapted
from (Newton et al., 2020) https://doi.org/10.3389/fsufs.2020.577723
Organic agriculture: Agriculture that focuses on production without the use of synthetic inputs and
does not allow the use of transgenic organisms.
Agricultural Biotechnology Glossary https://www.usda.gov/topics/biotechnology/biotechnology-
glossary

GBC Resolution 406.02 · 2022 · Online AGM (passed via GEM on August 18, 2022)

ADDED · 2022

406.02 · Training and Engagement of Oxen (2022)

Ministry of Cow Protection and Agriculture: Guidelines
[Guideline]

Whereas according to ISKCON’s Minimum Cow Protection and Agricultural Standards, section 2, IX an
ISKCON project is not allowed to acquire and breed milking cows if they don’t have a well-defined plan to
engage their oxen

Whereas the bull is the emblem of moral principles (SB 1.16.18 purport)

Whereas Lord Caitanya presented that the bull is our father because he helps with food production (CC Adi
17.153)

Whereas working oxen can multitask, provide service of many utilities. They can not only plough land, but
also transport pilgrims, guests, community members, and loads. In many places, they also grind spices and
grains

Whereas Padayatras offer natural engagement to the oxen and the spreading the holy names

Whereas there are ox-training teachers and courses, within and outside of ISKCON

Whereas most people have a connection with cows through dairy consumption, but very few have any
connection with working oxen

Whereas bulls represent 50% of the demographic of bovines to be cared for

Whereas many nations are indicating a need to reduce fossil fuel usage

Whereas Srila Prabhupada writes:

“So, take more land and engage them in agriculture, plowing by the bulls instead of a tractor. Bulls
can be engaged in plowing and transporting. Nice bullock carts village to village for preaching. Make
the farm the center and go ten miles this side, ten miles that side, ten miles this side, etc., with four
bullock carts. Sell books and preach and live peacefully on the farm. People used to engage the bull
for this purpose. So there was no problem with which way to utilize them. First of all, this artificial
way should be stopped, and the bulls should be engaged in plowing and transporting and smashing
the grains. To avoid machinery, petrol, machine oil, by nature’s way.”
(Letter to Balavanta, Bombay 3 January 1977)

Therefore, it is resolved that:

All National Bodies and Regional Bodies that have cow protection projects should establish regular training
and engagement of oxen, e.g., Padayatra parades, transportation, ploughing, etc. by Janmastami 2025.

[NOTE: The above updated resolutions and full standards of the Cow Protection and Agriculture Ministry
can be viewed here: Minimum Cow and Agriculture Standards

GBC Resolution 406.02 · 2022 · Online AGM (passed via GEM on July 20, 2022)

ADDED · 2022

407.01 · Mood of worship—Darsanas (2022)

ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry: Standards
[Governing law]

Whereas in 2021 the GBC made the following statement:

That the GBC reaffirms the mood of worship established by Srila Prabhupada, which is to be
followed in all ISKCON centers, is the mood of awe and reverence.

All worship conducted in ISKCON centers, both regular daily worship and occasional worship (such
as festivals), must be conducted according to this standard.

All ISKCON leaders are required to ensure that devotees and centers under their care understand
and implement worship according to these standards.

As such all practices that demonstrate a different mood of worship are not approved and must be
actively discouraged by leaders at all levels. This includes but is not limited to:

1. Devotee’s conduct in the presence of the deities.
2. The way devotees interact with the deities.
3. The manner in which devotees dress the deities, and
4. The different aspects of daily and festival services.

Whereas this resolution reaffirms Srila Prabhupada’s stated requirement of the mood of worship for
ISKCON centers as awe and reverence

Whereas it is necessary to define what this mood of worship looks like in the various aspects of deity
worship, so devotees understand proper standards

Whereas changing the appearance of deities conflicts with Srila Prabhupada’s stated mood of worship

Whereas every festival brings newer and more creative modifications to the appearance of the deities in
some ISKCON centers

Whereas according to Srila Prabhupada’s statement in Adi-lila 14.50, devotees should not divert their
attention to the worship of demigods.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

When observing festivals and dressing for daily darsana, the physical appearance of the deity must not be
modified. This includes, but is not limited to:

1. Covering the deities’ faces with masks, or otherwise obscuring the normal appearance or darsana.

2. Adding limbs to the deities, such as arms, legs, feet, etc.

3. Modifying the appearance of the deities’ eyes, either changing the colour or the direction they are
looking.

4. Dressing the deities as demigods

When temples have an interest in depicting pastimes of the Lord and His associates this may be achieved
via the use of dioramas, pictures, drama, and other means.

GBC Resolution 407.06 · 2022 · Online AGM (passed via GEM on October 14, 2022)
Source: resolutions-2022.md | 2022
ADDED · 2022

408.01 · GBC Inquiry regarding Child Abuse at Sridham Mayapur and (2022)

Ministry of Education: Gurukula
[Action order]

Vrndavana — 2022

Whereas it has been brought to the attention of the GBC Body that there were lapses in the implementation
of sufficient child protection measures in the ISKCON Mayapur and Vrndavana Schools

Whereas it is imperative to first identify, by way of an inquiry, the causes of such a lapse in the current
governance and system setup for child protection and, subsequently, to put in place measures to avert
such lapses from being repeated in the ISKCON Mayapur and Vrndavana schools

Whereas such an inquiry shall not preclude the formation or functioning of other committees with respect to
improving child protection within ISKCON.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

The GBC conducts an inquiry to identify the lapses in the implementation of child protection measures at
ISKCON Mayapur and Vrndavana schools, details of which are set out below as follows:

1. Scope of enquiry

a. This inquiry will be limited to ISKCON schools with specific focus on examining their current
organisational structures and legal frameworks required for child protection and to assess
the current risks in respect of the same.
b. Identify the root causes of governance shortcomings in the ISKCON Mayapur Gurukula by
interviewing relevant members of the CPO, GBC Zonal Secretaries, Mayapur temple
leadership, the current school leadership, and any other parties that may have been
connected, directly or indirectly, to the ISKCON Mayapur Gurukula, review the
documentation that governs the relationship between these entities and similarly review the
governance arrangements and documentation for ISKCON Vrndavana Gurukula.
c. Ascertain whether the governance shortcomings identified above are likely to be replicated
across other ISKCON school settings; this will likely include wider interviews and
documentation review.
d. Review the structural and legal relationship between the different layers of ISKCON with
governance of schools and the CPO.
e. Ancillary to the above review will be the Inquiry’s access to and study of the CPO Guidelines
as they relate to scope as outlined in items a–d above.

2. Desired Outcomes

a. Phase one shall entail collating the findings of the Inquiry and making specific written
recommendations to the GBC Body in order to remedy the identified shortcomings and
areas of improvement for implementation by relevant bodies; and
b. Phase two will be supporting implementation of the adopted recommendations of the Inquiry.
c. Identifying qualified resources who could help implement the approved recommendations.
d. Commissioning mandatory annual child protection audits for every school. These audits
should be carried out by professionals (with no conflict of interest) and their reports should
be made public.

3. Proposed team

a. Individuals with extensive school safeguarding and inspection experience will be appointed
at the discretion of the inquiry coordinator; The team members shall be independent from
ISKCON management and have no conflict of interest.
b. The Avanti Schools’ legal advisors are available for consultation where necessary.
c. Other volunteers for management, communication, and administration to support this
process will be recruited as needed.
d. Navina Krishna dasa will coordinate the inquiry.

4. Funding

Navina Krishna dasa has kindly agreed to raise the funding for the following:

a. Team consultation fees
b. Legal consultation fees.

5. Timeline

First phase report is to be presented to the GBC Body within 8 weeks after whatever preliminary
information is requested by the team is provided to them.

6. Action items

Upon approval of the GBC Body, the following actions need to be completed:

a. The GBC directs its secretary, and the CPO Director to assist in this endeavor and provide
the information timely as requested by the inquiry team.
b. By and before 30th December 2022, GBC members on the India Bureau, headed by Gopal
Krishna Goswami, procure the India Bureau’s formal resolution and commitment to support
the completion of this inquiry.
c. By and before 2nd January 2023, GBC Zonal secretaries (Jayapataka Swami, Gopal
Krishna Goswami, Bhakti Purushottama Swami, Hrdaya Caitanya dasa and Anuttama dasa)
and Indian Bureau representatives (Devakinandan dasa, Basu Ghosh dasa and Dayaram
dasa) with authority over Mayapur must procure the Mayapur Executive Board (MEB) formal
resolution and commitment to support the completion of this inquiry.
d. MEB resolution should include assigning a dedicated co-director to arrange and assure
cooperation from the Mayapur management structure for the timely completion of the inquiry.
e. The co-director should procure by 15th January 2023 the preliminary information stated
below so that the formal inquiry can ensue.
f. By and before 8th January 2023, GBC Zonal secretaries, and Indian Bureau representatives
with authority over Vrndavana must procure the Vrndavana Executive Board (VEB) formal
resolution and commitment to support the completion of this inquiry.
g. VEB resolution should include assigning the temple president to arrange and assure
cooperation from the Vrndavana management structure for the timely completion of the
inquiry.
h. The temple president should procure by 31st January 2023 the preliminary information
stated below so that the formal inquiry can ensue.

7. Preliminary information

a. Provide a copy of all resolutions passed by the GBC body and local management with
respect to child protection at these schools.
b. The existing CPO guidelines that needed to be adhered to at these centers.
c. Provide a copy of any scheme of delegation or legal or financial arrangement that connects
the schools to ISKCON. This could be property leases, MOUs, management agreements,
governing articles, and so on.
d. Provide a copy of the child protection, health and safety, whistleblowing, complaints,
grievance policies that the school has adopted.
e. Provide a list of the names and contact details of the governors of the school and
principal/head teacher.
f. Provide a copy of any scheme of delegation or legal framework that sets out the relationship
between the international CPO to the GBC body.
g. Provide a copy of any scheme of delegation or legal framework that that sets out the
relationship between the local CPT to the GBC body and to the international CPO.
h. Who owns the land and buildings upon which the school operates?
i. What is the legal entity that owns the school? Please provide the governing documents for
this entity (articles of association and memorandum, trust document etc.).
j. What is the legal entity that operates the school? (If different from the owner). Please
provide the governing documents for this entity (articles of association and memorandum,
trust document etc.).
[Note: This report has been completed and is currently being reviewed by the GBC]

GBC Resolution 408.01 · 2022 · GBC Virtual Meetings (passed on December 14, 2022
Source: resolutions-2022.md | 2022
ADDED · 2022

430.01 · Committees and Subcommittees: Change of Category (2022)

Committees: Establishing committees
[Statement]

Whereas it is required for the smooth functioning of the GBC meetings that the Rules of Order are up to
date and available to all members

Whereas the Rules of Order have not been updated for many years

Whereas the following has been established as a rule of order:

COMMITTEES AND SUBCOMMITTEES

The GBC Body may establish committees with such powers as appropriate.
l. POWERS OF COMMITTEE

1. A committee may have the power:

a To make decisions on matters as may be recommended by the GBC.

b To act on behalf of the GBC in some areas as fixed by the GBC.

c To submit reports or recommendations to the GBC as directed.

ll. WORKING OF COMMITTEES

1. The officers should be appointed by the GBC Body.

2. The committee shall elect its Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and Secretary if any of them is not
appointed by the GBC.

3. The office bearers shall perform their duties within the limits defined by the GBC and shall
remain answerable to the parent body.

lll. APPOINTMENT OF SUBCOMMITTEES

4. A committee may appoint a subcommittee to deal with some specific branch of the work
insofar as the committee has not been barred from delegating its powers. The following shall
apply:

a The powers delegated to the subcommittee can be revoked or rescinded at any time
by the committee.
b The subcommittee must report to the committee.
c The subcommittee ceases to function as soon as the purpose for which it is created
is accomplished.

lV. POWERS AND DUTIES OF SUBCOMMITTEES

1. A subcommittee’s powers and duties shall be clearly stated by the appointing body, paying
special attention to the following:

a. Power to recommend or advise
b. Power to act, spend, etc.
c. Frequency of meetings
d. Source of funds, if applicable

V. COMMITTEE REPORT

1. Each standing committee’s Chairman shall submit a written report to the GBC Body at the
outset of the yearly meeting as to the work, program, and participation of the committee
during the previous year.

Whereas a rule of order is defined as: “Procedures for the functioning of the GBC Body”

Whereas an Administrative Order is defined as: “Orders by which an administrative wing or branch of
ISKCON with specific functions is created. A ministry or other functional unit that has an existence beyond
the scope of the individuals performing the task”

Whereas this resolution is not a Rule of Order, but an Administrative Order.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

The resolution “Committees and sub-committees” is re-categorized as an Administrative order.

441.02 · Amendment to the worship at Vaiṣṇava samadhis (2022)

Vaiṣṇava Memorial Standing Committee: Regulations
[Governing law]

Whereas in December 2020 the GBC passed the resolution “Worship at Vaisnava samadhis — 2020”
which states:

1. There will be no daily worship required, either individually or collectively, offered to any Vaisnava in
any Vaisnava Memorial Park in Mayapur. However, individuals may occasionally offer incense,
flowers or prasadam remnants.

2. A modest ceremony honoring a departed Vaisnava may be organized on the appearance and
disappearance days of the departed Vaisnava. This function may include offering bhoga, arati,
puspanjali, glorification of the departed Vaisnava and a feast.

3. In accordance with existing ISKCON Law there will be no murti (deity) of any departed Vaisnava.
There may be a photo of the departed Vaisnava and where applicable a pair of shoes or other
similar paraphernalia.

4. This resolution is retroactive and applies to all existing samadhis located anywhere on ISKCON land
in Mayapur.

Whereas the Vaishnava Memorial Standing Committee (VMSC) proposes that such a resolution is
applicable everywhere.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

The resolution “Worship at Vaiṣṇava samadhis — 2020” in regard to the worship at Vaiṣṇava samadhis is
applicable worldwide and is amended to read:

1. No daily worship, either individual or collective, is required to be offered to any Vaisnava in any
Vaisnava Memorial. Still, individuals may offer incense, flowers or prasadam remnants.

2. A modest ceremony honoring a departed Vaisnava may be organized on the appearance and
disappearance days of the departed Vaisnava. This function may include offering bhoga, arati,
puspanjali, glorification of the departed Vaisnava and a feast. This ceremony must be significantly
less elaborate than the worship offered to Srila Prabhupada at that ISKCON center.

3. ISKCON assumes no responsibility for the worship, now or in the future.

4. In accordance with existing ISKCON Law there will be no murti (deity) of any departed Vaisnava
established or worshipped on ISKCON property. There may be a photo of the departed Vaisnava
and where applicable a pair of shoes or other paraphernalia.

5. This resolution is retroactive and applies to all existing samadhis located on ISKCON property
anywhere in the world. Any ISKCON center with an existing deity (as of 28 March 2022) of a
departed Vaishnava may apply for exemption via the ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry website and
this request will be forwarded to the GBC body for consideration.

407.02 · Installing Laksmi-Nrsimha and Balaji in Guntur (2023)

ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry: Installations
[Statement]

Whereas ISKCON Guntur, India, has applied to install deities of Laksmi-Nrsimha and Balaji.

Whereas ISKCON Law “Regulation of installations — 2017” states:

For any applications for deities apart from those given by Srila Prabhupada, i.e., Radha-Krsna;
Jagannatha, Baladeva, Subhadra; Gaura-Nitai (or Panca-tattva); and salagram silas; the IDWM
requires executive input. Therefore, for any application that includes Krsna-Balarama or Sita Rama
Laksmana Hanumana, the IDWM will consult with the GBC Executive Committee for approval. Any
deities, apart from the aforementioned, must be approved by the GBC Body before the IDWM can
issue a Certificate of Readiness for installing deities.

Whereas in 2011 ISKCON Guntur was gifted land with the condition of installing deities of Nrsimhadeva
and Balaji.

Whereas ISKCON Guntur installed deities of Jagannatha, Baladeva, and Subhadra and Radha-Krishna in
2014 under the direction of ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry’s India representatives.

Whereas the donor is pressuring the temple to install Laksmi-Nrsimha and Balaji as he feels his business is
suffering because he has not fulfilled his promise to the Lord.

Whereas ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry has expressed concerns about ISKCON submitting to the
pressure of a donor to install deities.

Whereas, understanding the difficultly faced by ISKCON Guntur in this situation and, after communicating
with the India Bureau and their indicating that they would like this installation to go ahead, ISKCON Deity
Worship Ministry is reluctantly willing to support the installation of these deities.

Whereas, ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry’s India representatives have assessed ISKCON Guntur as
having all the necessary brahmanas and other facilities and resources to care for the deities of Laksmi-
Nrsimha and Balaji.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry is hereby given permission to issue a Certificate of Readiness to ISKCON
Guntur for the deities of Laksmi-Nrsimha and Balaji.

GBC Resolution 445.22 · 2023 · GBC Virtual Meetings, passed January 18, 2023
Source: resolutions-2023.md | 2023
ADDED · 2023

453.03 · Brahma-gayatri Mantra in ISKCON – Varnasrama, Bhakti, Principle or (2023)

Sastric Advisory Council: Papers
[Governing law]

Detail — 2023

Whereas the GBC Body has been informed that there are instances within ISKCON where systems of
initiation have been instituted that differ significantly from the system followed by Śrīla Prabhupāda in terms
of the eligibility of a devotee for initiation, as well as the vows taken, and the mantras given at the time of
initiation.

And whereas at the request of the GBC Body, its Sastric Advisory Council (SAC) has extensively
researched the matter and presented a paper in their advisory capacity.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

1. Initiates’ vows at first initiation shall be, as Śrīla Prabhupāda required, to chant a minimum of
sixteen rounds daily of the maha-mantra:

Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare
Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare

as well as giving up intoxication, illicit sex, gambling and the eating of meat, fish, and eggs.

2. Initiating gurus at second initiation shall give the specific seven mantras that Śrīla Prabhupāda gave
to all initiates at what we call brahminical initiation or second initiation, and direct them to chant
them three times a day at three sandhyas (morning, mid-day, and evening).

3. Gurus and those who recommend initiation candidates shall not make any distinction of birth,
nationality, race, ethnicity, previous saṁskāra, marital status, gender, or classifications within the
varṇas (such as occupational livelihood) as to who would be eligible to take those vows and receive
those mantras in full at first and second initiation.

4. At the time of initiation, gurus should say, “As a member of ISKCON under the guidance and
leadership of the GBC Body, I give you initiation in the guru Parampara.”

Initiates must then take only the vows that Srila Prabhupada gave. Gurus may request, or instruct,
disciples to accept additional voluntary individual commitments, such as chanting extra rounds on
Ekadasi, or remaining loyal to ISKCON. However, such should be in the form of instructions or
guidelines and should not be included as an initiation requirement or vow.

[Footnotes to resolution]

The GBC is hereby publishing the Sastric Advisory Council paper entitled “Brahma-gayatri Mantra in
ISKCON -- Varnashrama, Bhakti, Principle or Detail?”

406.02 · Leasing of Cows Suspended (2024)

ISKCON Ministry of Cow Protection and Agriculture

Whereas currently according to the current Minimum Cow Protection Standards for ISKCON, section 2.IX.4
“Permitted”:

goal of cow protection, and if the lessee is legally bound to abide by all Cow Protection Standards,
ISKCON GBC Law 507 Minimum Cow Protection Standards 14 including, but not limited to,
arrangements made for lifetime protection of both cow and calf.

450.03 · ICPO Year Plan 2024-25 (2024)

ISKCON Child Protection Office: Other
[Action Order]

Whereas upon completion of the discussions held on 1st and 3rd March 2024 between Kamalesh Krishna
dasa, ICPO Director, and the GBC Body, Kamalesh Krishna dasa acknowledged shortcomings on his part,
and the GBC recognized the need for increased support of the International Child Protection Office, and
upon Kamalesh Krishna dasa’s request to have certainty on his continued role in the ICPO.

Therefore, it is resolved that:

1. For 2024-2025, the GBC has increased the ICPO’s budget to USD 54,000.

2. Kamalesh Krishna dasa is reappointed to serve as the ICPO Director for a period of one (1) year,
until March 1, 2025.

3. An interim Oversight Committee, as deemed necessary by the CPO Review and Working
Committees, shall be appointed by the GBC.

a. The primary and ongoing role of this Committee is to ensure CPO policies and procedures
are properly followed now and into the future.

b. The Oversight Committee shall not participate in any adjudications and/or investigations.

c. The Oversight Committee will report to the GBC EC.

4. During the upcoming year the following will be priorities for the ICPO:

a. The ICPO Director, is to prioritize the finalization of any pending cases, particularly those in
Bangladesh and Mayapur during this year. The GBC will assist in any way it can upon
request.

members (including several from India) that can be drawn from for any India cases. The

for future functioning.

panels in their respective regions comprising of trained and qualified members.

necessary, as determined by the Oversight Committee.

review from the Executive Secretariat Office (ESO), as well as the policies adopted from the 2023
Child Protection Review Committee and Working Group. The ICPO Director is directed to serve as
an advisor to those processes.

GBC Resolution 450.03 · 2024 · Annual General Meeting, passed March 9, 2024
Source: resolutions-2024.md | 2024
ADDED · 2025

407.01 · Teaching deity worship in ISKCON (2025)

ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry: Standards
[Governing law]

Whereas in 1996 the GBC established the following mandate for Ministers:

To establish the curriculum of his discipline and disseminate this knowledge throughout ISKCON.

Whereas for the sake of comparison, in 1997 the GBC passed the following resolution:

THAT the five-day seminar course established by the Global Book Distribution Minister is accepted
as the official training course for all ISKCON book distributors.
This course is to be taken by all:
1. New regular book distributors within the first twelve months of their book
2. distributing career, and
3. Regular book distributors by Gaura Purnima 1998, and
4. Part time book distributors are encouraged to take this course.
The Global Book Distribution Minister is responsible to supervise the standard and content of the
Book Distribution Graduate Course, promote it and ensure the requirements of this resolution are
met.

Whereas since 1999 the ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry (IDWM) has been actively developing and
presenting its curriculum globally and regularly presents courses in countries around the world;

Whereas 25+ years’ experience training devotees has shown us how to present curriculum in a way to
avoid an elitist pujari mentality, and also how to guide devotees to have a balanced approach to setting
realistic, sustainable standards of worship for ISKCON centers;

Whereas ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry is the GBC’s mandated agent for this discipline, and therefore the
most well positioned instrument to present authoritative teachings pertaining to deity worship within
ISKCON;

Whereas ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry now has more than 20 different courses on a wide range of deity
worship topics and topics related to deity worship;

Whereas when teaching a specific subject it is important that all facilitators address the same learning
objectives and present the same information, thus avoiding confusion amongst learners, and within
ISKCON;

Whereas a systematic curriculum, that is aligned with the GBC given mandate of IDWM, will enable
consistent standards of worship throughout ISKCON;

Whereas irregular presentations on deity worship are becoming more prevalent in ISKCON. Some of these
presentations even invalidate the teachings of our founder-acarya;

Whereas Srila Prabhupada stated:

The greatest danger to our movement will come when we manufacture and create our own process
for worshiping the deities. …follow it just to the exact standard as I have given you, that’s all.– Letter
to: Dhruvananda -- Bombay 4 January, 1973

You should only do what I tell you and show you in regard to deity worship, and never make
anything up or copy something you see somewhere else. – Personal instruction to Nanda Kumar
dasa

Whereas Srila Prabhupāda also explains:

So we have to accept religious principles from the leaders of the sampradāyas. Otherwise it is
useless. Sampradāya-vihīnā ye mantrās te viphalā matāḥ [Padma Purāṇa]: "If you do not accept
mantra initiation from the disciplic succession of the sampradāya, then it will be useless…. So
people are manufacturing religion without any reference to these authorities. – Śrīmad-Bhagavatam
6.1.34-39. December 19, 1970, Surat

Whereas in order to establish and disseminate a curriculum, Ministries need to regulate the curriculum and
who is teaching the curriculum

Therefore, it is resolved that:

1. All courses relating to deity worship in its entirety presented in ISKCON must be approved by
ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry. This includes and is not limited to courses on the following topics:

Temple deity worship
Home deity worship
Deity installations
Samskaras
Observing festivals

2. Only devotees who are mandated by ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry may present or teach courses
on deity worship and deity worship related matters. Devotees who are authorised by IDWM to teach
deity worship will have appropriate teaching qualifications and be graduates from an IDWM
approved course on the topic they are teaching. IDWM may also from time to time approve
devotees to teach various topics without them having to complete an IDWM approved course.

3. All IDWM approved courses must offer IDWM approved certificates.

GBC Resolution 407.01 · 2025 · Annual General Meeting, passed February 23, 2025

ADDED · 2025

407.01 · Moving large deities (2025)

ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry: Regulations
[Governing law]

Preamble: The question occasionally arises as to whether or not it is acceptable to move large marble
deities. In certain circumstances deities may be moved, but this cannot be done whimsically. The deities
can only be moved for the right reasons. As explained by Srila Prabhupada, to move the deities for profit, or
to get a prestigious building is not the correct motive. Sometimes it may happen that moving deities is
unavoidable, in situations where natural disaster is threatening the deity, or to protect the deity from harm.
Sometimes it may also be necessary to move deities when an ISKCON center cannot care for the deities.
However, the general principle is that large deities should never be moved once the worship has begun.
This proposal addresses this question.

Whereas Srila Prabhupada was generally strongly opposed to the moving of deities, as the following
excerpt demonstrates:

It is not very good policy to move the deities once they have been installed. – Letter to Karandhara,

GBC Resolution 407.01 · 2025 · Annual General Meeting, passed February 23, 2025
Source: resolutions-2025.md | 2025
ADDED · 2025

407.03 · Observing festivals on the day of the correct tithi (2025)

ISKCON Deity Worship Ministry: Guidelines
[Guideline]

Whereas it has been reported that at some ISKCON centers, major festivals are sometimes observed on
days and times that are convenient for the congregation to attend and not observed on the days specified
for the observance in the Vaishnava Calendar;

Whereas while encouraging the congregation to participate in temple celebrations is certainly important,
observing these occasions on the designated day and time is most auspicious and recommended for all
devotees. The full-time practicing devotees and others who are able to attend the temple on those most
auspicious days and times to participate in the observance should as far as possible be facilitated to do so;

And whereas Srila Prabhupada emphasized observing festivals according to the designated days and
times as practiced in our sampradaya

Therefore, it is resolved that:

All ISKCON centres are encouraged to:

1. Observe all major festivals on their actual dates;
2. Once such an observance is held, additional observances of the same nature may also be held on
subsequent days and times more convenient for the congregational devotees to attend to keep
them inspired in devotional service. Additional observances may be simple or elaborate, depending
on the need.
3. Devotees are encouraged to fast on those actual dates according to Srila Prabhupada’s instructions
and GBC guidelines

The following is the list of festivals with their observance timings that are to be considered as major
festivals as per the above rule:

Sri Gaur Purnima (Evening)
Sri Rama Navami (Noon)
Sri Nrsimha Caturdasi (Evening)
Sri Balaram Purnima (Noon)
Sri Krishna Janmastami (Midnight)
Srila Prabhupada’s Appearance Day (Noon)
Sri Radhastami (Noon)
Srila Prabhupada’s Disappearance Day (Noon)
Sri Nityananda Trayodasi (Noon)

GBC Resolution 407.03 · 2025 · Annual General Meeting, passed February 23, 2025
Source: resolutions-2025.md | 2025
ADDED · 2025

411.02 · Temple kirtana guidelines (2025)

ISKCON Harinama Sankirtana Ministry: Kirtana standards
[Guideline]

Whereas there is a need in ISKCON for clarity in temple room kirtana guidelines.

Therefore it is resolved that:
The GBC approves the Temple Kirtana Guidelines as appended below. It shall be a living document that
may be amended as required by the ISKCON Kirtana Ministry, provided such amendments are first
circulated on the GBC email conference, and no objections are received within thirty days.

Temple Kirtana Guidelines

Based on the teachings of His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada Founder-Acharya of
The International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON)

Preamble: Devotees are encouraged to chant wholeheartedly in all temple kirtanas. Managers should do
their best to implement these standards for the pleasure of Srila Prabhupada and the Vaisnavas.
Participants are encouraged to follow these guidelines under the guidance of the local ISKCON
management team in a mood of loving cooperation.

Golden Guidelines:
1. Always consider, “Is this kirtana pleasing to Srila Prabhupada?”
2. The most important sound in the kirtana is the congregational chanting, which the instruments
should never overpower.
3. Kirtana should be attractive, welcoming, and inclusive.

Kirtana Leaders
1. Preferably, ISKCON initiated devotees in good standing, chanting at least 16 daily rounds and
following the four regulative principles. Or, if not initiated, at least following the four regulative
principles, accept Srila Prabhupada’s teachings and regularly chanting japa.
2. Appearance: Preferably clean and simple dress, face shaven, with Gaudiya Vaisnava tilaka. For
men, dhoti, kurta, and chaddar are encouraged. For women, saris or gopi dress and shawl are
encouraged. Shorts and other revealing clothes are discouraged.

Mantras
1. During temple arati kirtanas, first chant Srila Prabhupada’s Pranam Mantras, Panca Tattva Maha
Mantra(s), and then the Hare Krishna Maha Mantra, which should be the primary mantra in every
kirtana.
2. Chant the Nrsimha Prayers after each arati.
3. The following may occasionally be sung:
4. Bhajans, mantras from BBT songbooks, and songs from Gaudiya Vaisnava Acharyas.
5. Govinda Jaya Jaya Gopala Jaya Jaya
6. haraye namah krsna yadavaya namah / gopala govinda rama sri-madhusudana
7. Jaya Sacinandana
8. Nitai Gouranga
9. Jaya Prabhupada
10. The chanting of Srimati Radharani’s holy names in isolation from Krishna may be chanted for a few
minutes on Radhastami.
11. It is recommended that no words or syllables be added or subtracted.
12. Kirtana leaders should avoid breaking up the response chanting from the congregation according to
material designations ie: Male/Female.
13. Breaking the mantra into smaller parts is not encouraged.
14. The chanting should be done first by the leader and then by the congregation. While the leader is
chanting, interjections by the congregation of “Chaitanya!”, “Nityananda!”, “Hare Hare!”, etc, are not
encouraged.
15. Chanting the deities’ names towards the end of the arati kirtana is optional, as they may be glorified
during the Prema Dhvani prayers.
16. Prema Dhvani mantras should be recited at the end of the arati kirtana.

Mangala Arati
1. During Mangala arati, the “morning melody” should be sung.

Instruments
1. The instruments should support the chanting and never overpower the sound of the
chanting. Chanting should always be heard.
2. Instrument players should learn the art of playing the instruments both loudly and powerfully as well
as softly and sweetly.
3. Mridanga players should aspire to play authentic beats according to parampara. Modern
adaptations derived from modern dance music, etc., should be avoided.
4. During the kirtanas and the arati, the following instruments should be played: mridanga and
kartalas. Whompers and gong may also be played.
5. The arati kirtana ends with the chanting of the Prema Dhvani mantras.
6. Additional instruments (harmonium, etc.) may be added after the arati kirtanas with the approval of
the local management team.
7. While devotees are encouraged to practice the musical instruments to play them nicely for the
pleasure of the deities, the temple room is not an appropriate venue. Practicing should be done
outside the temple room.
8. The sound of the mridanga should not be eclipsed by other instruments. Therefore, various drums
and other instruments that drown out the sound of the mridangas and the chanting are not
encouraged.
9. Health considerations of overly loud drums are essential considerations as some devotees develop
migraines and even permanent ear damage.

Singing
1. Alap is a classical Hindustani musical technique in which the mantra is lengthened, and additional
ornaments are added. This technique was not utilized in ISKCON kirtana during Srila Prabhupada’s
physical presence. Alap is not generally appropriate during Arati kirtanas. Other than arati kirtanas,
it may be permitted with the approval of the local management.
2. For those with the capacity, “Rama” should be pronounced as spelled, not “Ramo.”
3. Everyone, including instrument players, should also sing in response, as the congregational
chanting is the essence of kirtana.

Sound Systems
4. The sound system should be set at a modest volume. Louder is not better. 85 dBA is a reasonable
amount.
5. Refer to GBC Resolution of 2014: 313: Sound Systems Guideline:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tAiBDMTinpnKf9jWVqer0prTequqp-
M7eaBHZtANZ5s/edit?usp=sharing
6. Only one microphone is recommended to be used during kirtanas.
7. All electronic gadgets should be in silent mode or connected to headphones for personal listening.

Dancing
1. Dancing should be graceful, in a traditional Gaudiya Vaishnava style. Approved dances include, but
are not limited to, the Swami Step, forward and back, and jumping.
2. Participants should always endeavor to face the deity.

Dancing Safely
1. Dancing should not endanger the physical safety of the participants.
2. Lifting devotees into the air can cause injuries and may not be an appropriate mood.
3. Spinning around should be done with care.

Deities
1. Deities carried into the temple by congregational devotees should be treated with respect and care
according to the principles set by the Deity Worship Ministry. They should not be rocked, jumped up
and down, or spun around in circles.

411.02 · Temple kirtana guidelines infographic (2025)

Therefore, it is resolved that:

ISKCON Kirtana Ministry will make the Temple Kirtana Guidelines available as an infographic on its website
and circulate the link on the Leadership Discussions email conference by August 1, 2025.
ISKCON centers are encouraged to print and post the Temple Kirtana Guidelines in or near ISKCON
temple rooms by September 1, 2025.

GBC Resolution 411.02 · 2025 · Annual General Meeting, passed February 23, 2025
Source: resolutions-2025.md | 2025
ADDED · 2025

414.01 · Sannyasa assessment and approval: amendments (2025)

Ministry of Sannyasa Services: Policy manual
[Governing law]

Whereas resolution 57/1988 states:

"That a brahmacari be considered for sannyasa only if he has actually strictly followed his vows for
at least ten years and is at least forty years old. In exceptional cases, a man may be awarded
sannyasa before the age of forty by a 2/3 majority vote of the GBC Body. To take sannyasa at the
age of 50, one must have been on a waiting list for two years; at 45, three years; at 40, four years,
and at 35, five years”.

Whereas the methods of evaluating candidates, expectations of them, means of training, and assessment
of readiness to take sannyasa, is evolving as per the experience of the Sannyasa Ministry;

Whereas conflicts may be avoided by modifying the current system;

Whereas by modifying the current system, time and energy may be saved at the GBC level;

Whereas by including accomplishments in the process, candidates may be inspired to offer more valuable
service to Srila Prabhupada’s mission

Therefore, it is resolved that:

Resolution 57/1988 be replaced by:

The following is the official policy of the Sannyasa Ministry:

1. The Sannyasa Ministry will evaluate the qualities and accomplishments of applicants and thus
determine whether a devotee can become a "potential candidate" to possibly become a "sannyasa
candidate" to take sannyasa.

Such qualities may include but are not limited to:

• Cooperation with authorities.
• Demonstrates a practical understanding of the concept of "Unity in Diversity".
• Ability to present Krsna consciousness to different levels of people and devotees and
effectively increase others’ level of commitment to Krsna consciousness.
• Demonstrating exemplary sadhana
• Having a clear grasp of the philosophy and mission of Lord Caitanya Mahaprabhu as
presented by Srila Prabhupada.
• Ability and sincerity to practice what one preaches.
• Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of devotees and authorities.

Accomplishments may include but are not limited to:

• Demonstrating an ability to create a preaching field, expand it and maintain it without much
outside assistance, thereby exhibiting self-reliance.
• Creating an atmosphere of cooperation between devotees on all levels of Krsna
consciousness.
• Leading a balanced life of health, preaching, sadhana, and relationships with devotees.

2. A candidate in order to be eligible to take sannyasa must be at least 40 years old.
3. The minimum number of years each devotee will be confirmed as a "potential sannyasa candidate"
is one year.
4. When a potential candidate is found to be qualified, they may become a sannyasa candidate for one
year.
5. After that one year, the sannyasa candidate may be recommended to take sannyasa.

Procedure:

1. The Team for Assessing Sannyasa Candidates (TASC) committee accepts applications for
sannyasa once annually.
2. Upon acceptance, applicants have their supporting documents reviewed by secretaries to ensure
compliance with Sannyasa Ministry guidelines.
3. A Pre-Submit process begins by the application secretary wherein the Sannyasa Ministry receives
feedback from the various devotees the candidate has mentioned as references in the application.
4. TASC evaluates the candidate based on the feedback received from various devotees and also the
TASC requests the candidate to give class on a verse, which is also heard by the TASC members.
5. TASC members then discuss whether to accept him as a potential candidate or whether further
evidence of eligibility is required.
6. Once accepted as a potential sannyasa candidate the candidate has his duties and training
prescribed by the TASC, according to Sannyasa Ministry guidelines.
7. The TASC submits a yearly list of all newly accepted potential sannyasa candidates to the
Sannyasa Standing Committee.
8. Potential sannyasa candidates fulfill all duties and assignments outlined by the TASС, TSCS (Team
for Serving Candidates of Sannyasa), and the Sannyasa Mission committee for a minimum of one
year.
9. At the end of each year, their training period is reviewed and, if necessary, renewed as deemed
necessary by the TASC, following Sannyasa Ministry guidelines for sufficient improvement.
10. The TASC reviews the performance of potential sannyasa candidates, providing feedback for
improvement to them, based on the feedback received from their recommending GBC, Guru,
sannyasa mentors, and prospective sannyasa gurus, travel reports, mission reports, and
Sannaysa college, etc.
11. Failure to comply with TASC guidance incurs a warning, followed by a second warning, and
eventual removal from the list of potential sannyasa candidates.
12. The Sannyasa Standing Committee reserves the right to remove a potential candidate at any time,
based on TASC advice or their own simple majority decision.
13. When the TASC is satisfied with overall progress of the potential sannyasa candidate he is then
proposed to be accepted as a candidate to the Sannyasa Standing Committee, which then votes by
a 2/3 majority.
14. A list of sannyasa candidates is presented to the GBC at the next AGM for their vote, with a
minimum recommended waiting period of one year.
15. The GBC has the authority to waive or extend the waiting period by a simple majority vote.

442.01 · Mandate of the GBC Executors and Property Oversight Committee (2025)

GBC Executors Property Oversight Committee: Committee
[Governing law]

(GEPOC) – 2025

Whereas the GBC, acting on concerns raised amongst its members, reviewed the mandate of the GBC
Executors Property and Oversight Committee (GEPOC) and, particularly, its Schedule of Authority, which
was established in a 2022 GBC resolution to revitalize property protection in ISKCON;

Whereas the Schedule of Authority, which defines the GEPOC’s role in ISKCON property protection,
currently empowers the GEPOC to approve the sale of properties outside of India without seeking approval
from the GBC;

Whereas it is imperative that the GBC, as ISKCON’s ultimate managing authority, possesses the power to
approve or reject the proposed mortgage, borrowing against, sale, transfer, encumbrance, disposal, or
alienation of ISKCON properties outside of India.

(Note that Srila Prabhupada’s Will explicitly specifies “…mortgaged, borrowed against, sold, transferred, or
in any way encumbered, disposed of, or alienated...” in respect of ISKCON properties.)

Therefore, it is resolved that:

The Schedule of Authority in respect of the sale, purchase, or mortgage of any ISKCON properties outside
India is hereby updated and amended as follows:

(a) The ISKCON Global Property Office (IGPO), which reports solely to the GEPOC, its direct oversight
authority, shall bring a proposal for any potential mortgage, borrowing against, sale, transfer, encumbrance,
disposal, or alienation of ISKCON properties to the GEPOC for review.

(b) The GEPOC shall process and review the IGPO’s report on the potential mortgage, borrowing against,
sale, transfer, encumbrance, disposal, or alienation of such a property and present its recommendations in
a report to the GBC for its approval or disapproval.

(c) For the avoidance of any doubt, the IGPO and GEPOC shall not process any purchases of ISKCON
properties.

GBC Resolution 442.01 · 2025 · AGM, passed February 23, 2025
